translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 163

sentences.zh: 【梁紀十九】　上章敦牂，一年。

translations.literal: [Liang Records 19] Shangzhang Dunzang; one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Records 19] Shangzhang Dunzang—one year in all.

sentences.zh: 太宗簡文皇帝上大寶元年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Jianwen, first year of Dabao (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen of Liang, first year of Dabao (

sentences.zh: 庚午，公元五五零年）

translations.literal: gengwu, 550 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengwu, AD 550)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥朔，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day xinhai, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, the new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 陳霸先發始興，至大庾嶺，蔡路養將二萬人軍於南野以拒之。

translations.literal: Chen Baxian set out from Shixing, reached Dayu Ridge; Cai Luyang led twenty thousand men and encamped at Nanye to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baxian marched from Shixing to Dayu Ridge. Cai Luyang led twenty thousand men and encamped at Nanye to block him.

sentences.zh: 路養妻侄蘭陵蕭摩訶，年十三，單騎出戰，無敢當者。

translations.literal: Luyang's wife's nephew Xiao Mohe of Lanling, thirteen years old, rode out alone to fight; none dared face him.
translations.idiomatic: Luyang's wife's nephew Xiao Mohe of Lanling was thirteen. He rode out alone to fight, and none dared face him.

sentences.zh: 杜僧明馬被傷，陳霸先救之，授以所乘馬。

translations.literal: Du Sengming's horse was wounded; Chen Baxian rescued him and gave him the horse he rode.
translations.idiomatic: Du Sengming's horse was wounded. Chen Baxian pulled him clear and gave him his own mount.

sentences.zh: 僧明上馬復戰，眾軍因而乘之。

translations.literal: Sengming mounted and fought again; the whole army pressed the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Sengming remounted and fought on; the whole army swept in behind him.

sentences.zh: 路養大敗，脫身走。

translations.literal: Luyang was routed badly and fled for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Luyang was routed and fled for his life.

sentences.zh: 霸先進軍南康，湘東王繹承製授霸先明威將軍、交州刺史。

translations.literal: Baxian advanced on Nankang; Prince of Xiangdong Yi, by regent's order, made Baxian Bright Might General and Jiaozhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Baxian advanced on Nankang. Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong, acting as regent, made Baxian bright might general and Jiaozhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，東魏進太原公高洋位丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事、大行台、齊郡王。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Eastern Wei advanced Prince of Taiyuan Gao Yang to Chancellor, Commander of All Forces Inside and Outside, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Prince of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Eastern Wei advanced Prince Gao Yang of Taiyuan to chancellor, commander of all forces inside and outside, recorder of the masters of writing, grand mobile headquarters, and prince of Qi commandery.

sentences.zh: 庚午，邵陵王綸至江夏，郢州刺史南平王恪郊迎，以州讓之，綸不受；

translations.literal: On gengwu, Prince of Shaoling Lun reached Jiangxia; Yingzhou Inspector Prince of Nanping Ke met him in the suburbs and offered the province; Lun would not accept;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Prince Lun of Shaoling reached Jiangxia. Yingzhou inspector Prince Ke of Nanping met him in the suburbs and offered the province; Lun refused;

sentences.zh: 乃推綸為假黃鉞，都督中外諸軍事，承製置百官。

translations.literal: they then made Lun acting bearer of the yellow battle-axe, Commander of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside, and by regent's order he installed the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: they then made Lun acting bearer of the yellow battle-axe, commander of all military affairs inside and outside, and by regent's order he installed the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 魏楊忠圍安陸，柳仲禮馳歸救之。

translations.literal: Wei Yang Zhong besieged Anlu; Liu Zhongli galloped back to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei general Yang Zhong besieged Anlu; Liu Zhongli galloped back to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 諸將恐仲禮至則安陸難下，請急攻之。

translations.literal: The generals feared that if Zhongli arrived Anlu would be hard to take and asked to attack at once.
translations.idiomatic: The generals feared that once Zhongli arrived Anlu would be hard to take and urged an immediate assault.

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「攻守勢殊，未可猝拔；

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Attack and defense differ in strength; it cannot be seized in a rush;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: "Attack and defense are not the same game; the city cannot be taken in a rush;

sentences.zh: 若引日勞師，表裡受敵，非計也。

translations.literal: if we draw out days and weary the army, we will be attacked inside and out—that is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: if we drag this out and weary the army, we will be caught between the city and relief—that is no plan at all.

sentences.zh: 南人多習水軍，不閒野戰，仲禮師在近路，吾出其不意，以奇兵襲之，彼怠我奮，一舉可克。

translations.literal: Southerners are practiced in river warfare and unskilled in field battle; Zhongli's army is on the near road—if we take them unawares with a surprise force, they weary while we are keen, and we can take them in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners train for river war, not field battle. Zhongli is close on the road. Take him unawares with a strike force—his men tired, ours eager—and we can break him at one blow.

sentences.zh: 克仲禮，則安陸不攻自拔，諸城可傳檄定也。

translations.literal: If we overcome Zhongli, Anlu will fall without attack and the other cities can be settled by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: Break Zhongli, and Anlu will fall without a siege; the rest of the cities can be settled by proclamation alone.

sentences.zh: 」乃選騎二千，銜枚夜進，敗仲禮於崇頭，獲仲禮及其弟子禮，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: " He then chose two thousand horsemen, advanced by night with gags in their mouths, defeated Zhongli at Chongtou, captured Zhongli and his younger brother Zili, and took all his troops prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: " He chose two thousand horsemen, advanced by night with gags in their mouths, routed Zhongli at Chongtou, captured Zhongli and his brother Zili, and took the whole force prisoner.

sentences.zh: 馬岫以安陸，別將王叔孫以竟陵，皆降於忠。

translations.literal: Ma Xiu surrendered Anlu; detached general Wang Shusun surrendered Jingling; both submitted to Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiu surrendered Anlu; detached general Wang Shusun surrendered Jingling; both submitted to Yang Zhong.

sentences.zh: 於是漢東之地盡入於魏。

translations.literal: Thus the lands east of the Han all passed into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the lands east of the Han all fell to Wei.

sentences.zh: 廣陵人來嶷說前廣陵太守祖皓曰：「董紹先輕而無謀，人情不附。

translations.literal: Lai Yi of Guangling said to former Guangling Administrator Zu Hao: "Dong Shaoxian is frivolous and without strategy; men's hearts do not cling to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Yi of Guangling said to former Guangling administrator Zu Hao: "Dong Shaoxian is frivolous and witless; no one truly follows him.

sentences.zh: 襲而殺之，此壯士之任耳。

translations.literal: Strike and kill him—that is a brave man's task.
translations.idiomatic: Strike and kill him—that is work fit for a brave man.

sentences.zh: 今欲糾帥義勇，奉戴府君。

translations.literal: I now wish to gather righteous volunteers and install you as our lord.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to gather righteous volunteers and set you up as our leader.

sentences.zh: 若其克捷，可立桓、文之勳；

translations.literal: If we succeed, we may establish merit like Huan and Wen;
translations.idiomatic: If we succeed, we may win merit like Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi;

sentences.zh: 必天未悔禍，猶足為梁室忠臣。

translations.literal: and even if Heaven has not yet turned from disaster, we may still suffice as loyal servants of the house of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: and even if Heaven has not yet turned from this disaster, we may still stand as loyal servants of Liang.

sentences.zh: 」皓曰：「此僕所願也。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "That is what this servant desires.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said: "That is what I desire.

sentences.zh: 」乃相與糾合勇士，得百餘人。

translations.literal: " They then together gathered brave men and got more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: " They gathered brave men together and mustered more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，襲廣陵，斬南兗州刺史董紹先；

translations.literal: On guiyou they raided Guangling and beheaded Southern Yanzhou Inspector Dong Shaoxian;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou they raided Guangling and beheaded Southern Yanzhou inspector Dong Shaoxian;

sentences.zh: 據城，馳檄遠近，推前太子舍人蕭勉為刺史，仍結東魏為援。

translations.literal: held the city, sent proclamations flying to far and near, made former crown prince attendant Xiao Mian inspector, and at once sought Eastern Wei as ally.
translations.idiomatic: seized the city, sent proclamations far and wide, made former crown prince attendant Xiao Mian inspector, and at once sought Eastern Wei as ally.

sentences.zh: 皓，□恆之之子；

translations.literal: Hao was the son of □ Hengzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Hao was the son of □ Hengzhi;

sentences.zh: 勉，勃之兄也。

translations.literal: Mian was Bo's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was the elder brother of Xiao Bo.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，景遣郭元建帥眾奄至，皓嬰城固守。

translations.literal: On yihai, Jing sent Guo Yuanjian leading troops in a sudden arrival; Hao closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Hou Jing sent Guo Yuanjian with troops in a sudden strike; Hao shut the gates and held firm.

sentences.zh: 二月，魏楊忠乘勝至石城，欲進逼江陵，湘東王繹遣舍人庾恪說忠曰：「察來伐叔而魏助之，何以使天下歸心！

translations.literal: In the second month, Wei Yang Zhong pressed his victory to Shicheng and wished to advance on Jiangling; Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent Gentleman-Attendant Yu Ke to persuade Zhong, saying: "Liang came to punish its uncle-rebel while Wei aids him—how will the empire turn its hearts to you!
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Yang Zhong of Wei pressed his victory to Shicheng and meant to advance on Jiangling. Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong sent gentleman-attendant Yu Ke to persuade him: "Liang marched to punish a rebel uncle while Wei aids him—how will the empire ever turn its hearts to you!

sentences.zh: 」忠遂停湕北。

translations.literal: " Zhong then halted north of the Jian.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Zhong then halted north of the Jian.

sentences.zh: 繹遣舍人王孝祀等送子方略為質以求和，魏人許之。

translations.literal: Yi sent Gentleman-Attendant Wang Xiaosi and others to deliver his son Fanglue as hostage to seek peace; the Wei men agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent gentleman-attendant Wang Xiaosi and others with his son Fanglue as hostage to sue for peace; Wei agreed.

sentences.zh: 繹與忠盟曰：「魏以石城為封，梁以安陸為界，請同附庸，並送質子，貿遷有無，永敦鄰睦。

translations.literal: Yi swore alliance with Zhong, saying: "Wei takes Shicheng as its fief, Liang takes Anlu as its border; let us both be vassal states, each send a hostage son, trade what we have and lack, and forever keep neighborly peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yi swore alliance with Yang Zhong: "Wei shall hold Shicheng as fief, Liang shall hold Anlu as border; let us both stand as vassal states, each send a hostage son, trade what we have and lack, and keep neighborly peace forever.

sentences.zh: 」忠乃還。

translations.literal: " Zhong then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Zhong then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宕昌王梁彌定為其宗人獠甘所襲，彌定奔魏，獠甘自立。

translations.literal: Prince of Dangchang Liang Miding was attacked by his clansman Liao Gan; Miding fled to Wei and Liao Gan set himself up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang Miding of Dangchang was attacked by his clansman Liao Gan; Miding fled to Wei and Liao Gan declared himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 羌酋傍乞鐵□據渠株川，與渭州民鄭五丑合諸羌以叛魏。

translations.literal: Qiang chieftain Pangqi Tiex□ held Qizhu River valley and, with Zheng Wuchou of Weizhou and the various Qiang, rebelled against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang chieftain Pangqi Tiex□ held the Qizhu River valley and, with Zheng Wuchou of Weizhou and the Qiang tribes, rebelled against Wei.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰使大將軍宇文貴、涼州刺史史寧討之，擒斬鐵□、五丑。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai sent Grand General Yuwen Gui and Liangzhou Inspector Shi Ning to campaign against them and captured and beheaded Tiex□ and Wuchou.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yuwen Tai sent grand general Yuwen Gui and Liangzhou inspector Shi Ning against them and captured and beheaded Tiex□ and Wuchou.

sentences.zh: 寧別擊獠甘，破之，獠甘將百騎奔生羌鞏廉玉。

translations.literal: Ning separately attacked Liao Gan, defeated him; Liao Gan led a hundred horsemen in flight to the raw Qiang Gong Lianyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ning separately attacked Liao Gan and broke him. Liao Gan fled with a hundred riders to the raw Qiang chieftain Gong Lianyu.

sentences.zh: 寧復納彌定於宕昌，置岷州於渠株川，進擊鞏廉玉，斬獠甘，虜廉玉送長安。

translations.literal: Ning again installed Miding in Dangchang, established Min province at Qizhu River valley, advanced to attack Gong Lianyu, beheaded Liao Gan, captured Lianyu, and sent him to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ning restored Miding in Dangchang, established Min province on the Qizhu River, advanced on Gong Lianyu, beheaded Liao Gan, captured Lianyu, and sent him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 侯景遣任約、於慶等帥眾二萬攻諸籓。

translations.literal: Hou Jing sent Ren Yue, Yu Qing, and others leading twenty thousand men to attack the various princely domains.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sent Ren Yue, Yu Qing, and others with twenty thousand men to attack the princely domains.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸欲救河東王譽，而兵糧不足，乃致書於湘東王繹曰：「天時地利，不及人和，況乎手足肱支，豈可相害！

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling Lun wished to rescue Prince of Hedong Yu but lacked troops and grain; he sent a letter to Prince of Xiangdong Yi, saying: "Heaven's season and earth's advantage are less than human harmony—how much more so for arms and legs of one body: how can they harm one another!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Shaoling wished to rescue Prince Yu of Hedong but lacked troops and grain. He wrote Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong: "Heaven's season and earth's advantage mean less than human harmony—how much less may the arms and legs of one body tear at each other!

sentences.zh: 今社稷危恥，創巨痛深，唯應剖心嘗膽，泣血枕戈，其餘小忿，或宜容貰。

translations.literal: Now the altars are in peril and shame; the wound is vast and the pain deep—we should only split our hearts and taste gall, weep blood and sleep on spears; other small resentments may sometimes be borne.
translations.idiomatic: The altars stand in peril and shame; the wound is vast and the pain runs deep. We should split our hearts and taste gall, weep blood and sleep on our spears. Other small resentments may sometimes be set aside.

sentences.zh: 若外難未除，家禍仍構，料今訪古，未或不亡。

translations.literal: If outer peril is not removed and inner calamity still builds, I reckon that from today back through antiquity, none have failed to perish.
translations.idiomatic: If outer enemies remain and kin still turn on kin, I reckon that from today back through antiquity, none have failed to perish.

sentences.zh: 夫征戰之理，唯求克勝；

translations.literal: In the logic of war, one seeks only victory;
translations.idiomatic: In war one seeks only victory;

sentences.zh: 至於骨肉之戰，愈勝愈酷，捷則非功，敗則有喪，勞兵損義，虧失多矣。

translations.literal: but in kin fighting, the more one wins the crueller it grows—triumph brings no merit, defeat brings mourning, troops are worn and righteousness harmed, and losses are many.
translations.idiomatic: but in war between kin, the more you win the crueller it grows. Triumph brings no merit, defeat brings mourning; troops are worn down, righteousness is harmed, and the losses mount.

sentences.zh: 侯景之軍所以未窺江外者，良為籓屏盤固，宗鎮強密。

translations.literal: The reason Hou Jing's army has not yet peered beyond the river is precisely that the princely screens are firm and the clan garrisons strong and close.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's army has not yet peered beyond the river precisely because the princely screens stand firm and the clan garrisons are strong and close.

sentences.zh: 弟若陷洞庭，不戢兵刃，雍州疑迫，何以自安，必引進魏軍以求形援。

translations.literal: If younger brother takes Dongting and does not sheathe blades, Yong province will be pressed with doubt—how will you keep yourself safe? You will surely bring in Wei troops to seek visible aid.
translations.idiomatic: If you take Dongting and do not sheathe your blades, Yong province will be pressed with doubt—how will you keep yourself safe? You will surely bring in Wei troops to seek visible aid.

sentences.zh: 弟若不安，家國去矣。

translations.literal: If younger brother is not secure, house and state are gone.
translations.idiomatic: If you are not secure, house and state are gone.

sentences.zh: 必希解湘州之圍，存社稷之計。

translations.literal: I earnestly hope you will lift the siege of Xiang province and preserve the plan for the altars.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly beg you to lift the siege of Xiang province and preserve the altars.

sentences.zh: 」繹復書，陳譽過惡不赦，且曰：「察引楊忠來相侵逼，頗遵談笑，用卻秦軍，曲直有在，不復自陳。

translations.literal: " Yi replied, setting forth Yu's crimes as beyond pardon, and said: "Cha brought Yang Zhong to invade and press us; I followed the talk and laughter and sent the Qin army back—right and wrong are clear; I need not argue further.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiao Yi replied, listing Yu's crimes as beyond pardon, and wrote: "You brought Yang Zhong to invade and press us. I followed the talk and sent the Qin army back—right and wrong are clear; I need not argue further.

sentences.zh: 臨湘旦平，暮便即路。

translations.literal: Linxiang will fall by morning; by evening I shall be on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Linxiang will fall by morning; by evening I shall be on the road.

sentences.zh: 」綸得書，投之於案，慷慨流涕曰「天下之事，一至於斯！

translations.literal: " Lun received the letter, cast it on the table, and with generous emotion wept, saying, "Affairs under Heaven have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: " Lun read the letter, threw it on the table, and wept: "Affairs under Heaven have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 湘州若敗，吾亡無日矣！

translations.literal: If Xiang province falls, my destruction is not far off!
translations.idiomatic: If Xiang province falls, my days are numbered!

sentences.zh: 侯景遣侯子鑒帥舟師八千，自帥徒兵一萬，攻廣陵，三日，克之，執祖皓，縛而射之，箭遍體，然後車裂以徇；

translations.literal: Hou Jing sent Hou Zijian leading eight thousand river troops; he himself led ten thousand foot soldiers to attack Guangling; in three days it fell; he seized Zu Hao, bound him and shot him until arrows covered his body, then quartered him by chariot as warning;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sent Hou Zijian with eight thousand river troops and himself led ten thousand foot soldiers against Guangling. In three days the city fell. He seized Zu Hao, bound him, shot him until arrows covered his body, then quartered him by chariot as warning;

sentences.zh: 城中無少長皆埋之於地，馳馬射而殺之。

translations.literal: within the city none young or old—all were buried in the earth, and horsemen galloped over them shooting and killing them.
translations.idiomatic: within the city none young or old were spared—they were buried in pits and horsemen galloped over them, shooting them down.

sentences.zh: 以子鑒為南兗州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: He made Zijian Southern Yanzhou Inspector, garrisoning Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zijian Southern Yanzhou inspector and garrisoned him at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 景還建康。

translations.literal: Jing returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以安陸王大春為東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Prince Dachun of Anlu was made Eastern Yangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Prince Dachun of Anlu was made Eastern Yangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 省吳州。

translations.literal: Wu province was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Wu province was abolished.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以尚書僕射王克為左僕射。

translations.literal: On yisi, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wang Ke was made Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, vice minister of the masters of writing Wang Ke was made left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，東魏以尚書令高隆之為太保。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Eastern Wei made Minister of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Eastern Wei made minister of the masters of writing Gao Longzhi grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 宣城內史楊白華進據安吳，侯景遣於子悅等帥眾攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Xuancheng Interior Secretary Yang Baihua advanced and held Anwu; Hou Jing sent Yu Ziyue and others leading troops to attack but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng interior secretary Yang Baihua advanced and held Anwu. Hou Jing sent Yu Ziyue and others against him but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 東魏行台辛術將兵入寇，圍陽平，不克。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Mobile Headquarters Xin Shu led troops in invasion, besieged Yangping, and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei mobile headquarters commander Xin Shu invaded, besieged Yangping, and could not take it.

sentences.zh: 侯景納上女溧陽公主，甚愛之。

translations.literal: Hou Jing took the emperor's daughter, Princess of Liyang, in marriage and loved her greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing married the emperor's daughter, the Princess of Liyang, and doted on her.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲申，景請上禊宴於樂游苑，帳飲三日。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiashen, Jing asked the emperor to a spring purification feast in Leyou Garden; they drank under tents for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiashen, Hou Jing invited the emperor to a spring purification feast in Leyou Garden; they drank under tents for three days.

sentences.zh: 上還宮，景與公主共據御床，南面並坐，群臣文武列坐侍宴。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the palace, Jing and the princess together occupied the imperial couch, sat facing south side by side, and civil and military officials arrayed themselves in seats to attend the feast.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace, Hou Jing and the princess shared the imperial couch, sat facing south side by side, while civil and military officials arrayed themselves to attend the feast.

sentences.zh: 庚申，東魏進丞相洋爵為齊王。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Eastern Wei advanced Chancellor Yang's rank to Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Eastern Wei advanced Chancellor Gao Yang's rank to prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 臨川內史始興王毅等擊莊鐵，鄱陽王范遣其將巴西侯瑱救之，毅等敗死。

translations.literal: Linchuan Interior Secretary Prince Yi of Shixing and others attacked Zhuang Tie; Prince of Poyang Fan sent his general Hou Zhen of Baxi to rescue him; Yi and the rest were defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Linchuan interior secretary Prince Yi of Shixing and others attacked Zhuang Tie. Prince Fan of Poyang sent his general Hou Zhen of Baxi to rescue him. Yi and the rest were defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽世子嗣與任約戰於三章，約敗走；

translations.literal: Poyang Heir Si fought Ren Yue at Sanzhang; Yue was defeated and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Poyang heir Si fought Ren Yue at Sanzhang. Yue was beaten and fled;

sentences.zh: 嗣因徙鎮三章，謂之安樂柵。

translations.literal: Si then moved his garrison to Sanzhang and called it Anle Palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Si then moved his camp to Sanzhang and called it Anle Palisade.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚辰朔，湘東王繹以上甲侯韶為長沙王。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day gengchen, Prince of Xiangdong Yi made Senior Armorer Hou Shao Prince of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengchen, the new moon, Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong made senior armorer Hou Shao prince of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 丙午，侯景請上幸西州，上御素輦，侍衛四百餘人，景浴鐵數千，翼衛左右。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Hou Jing asked the emperor to visit Xizhou; the emperor rode a plain carriage with more than four hundred guards; Jing had several thousand armored men flanking left and right.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Hou Jing asked the emperor to visit Xizhou. The emperor rode a plain carriage with more than four hundred guards; Hou Jing had several thousand armored men flanking him left and right.

sentences.zh: 上聞絲竹，淒然泣下，命景起舞，景亦請上起舞。

translations.literal: The emperor heard silk and bamboo music and wept desolately; he ordered Jing to dance, and Jing also asked the emperor to dance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard music and wept. He ordered Hou Jing to dance; Hou Jing asked the emperor to dance as well.

sentences.zh: 酒闌坐散，上抱景於床曰：「我念丞相！

translations.literal: When the wine was spent and the seats dispersed, the emperor embraced Jing on the couch and said: "I miss the Chancellor!
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was spent and the guests dispersed, the emperor embraced Hou Jing on the couch and said: "I miss the Chancellor!

sentences.zh: 」景曰：「陛下如不念臣，臣何得至此！

translations.literal: " Jing said: "If Your Majesty did not miss your servant, how could your servant have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: " Hou Jing said: "If Your Majesty did not miss me, how could I have come to this!

sentences.zh: 」逮夜乃罷。

translations.literal: " Only at night did it end.
translations.idiomatic: " Only at night did it end.

sentences.zh: 時江南連年旱蝗，江、揚尤甚，百姓流亡，相與入山谷、江湖，采草根、木葉、菱芡而食之，所在皆盡，死者蔽野。

translations.literal: At this time the south of the Yang had drought and locusts for years in succession; Jiang and Yang suffered especially; common people fled, entering together into valleys and rivers and lakes to gather grass roots, tree leaves, water chestnuts and gorgon seeds to eat; wherever they went all was exhausted and the dead covered the wild.
translations.idiomatic: The south of the Yang had suffered drought and locusts for years; Jiang and Yang were worst hit. People fled into valleys and along rivers and lakes, eating grass roots, leaves, water chestnuts, and gorgon seeds until nothing remained; the dead covered the countryside.

sentences.zh: 富室無食，皆鳥面鵠形，衣羅綺，懷金玉，俯伏床帷，待命聽終。

translations.literal: Rich houses had no food; all were bird-faced and swan-bodied, dressed in gauze and silk, carrying gold and jade, lying prostrate by bed curtains awaiting the end.
translations.idiomatic: Even rich households went hungry. Men were gaunt as birds and storks, still dressed in gauze and silk, gold and jade at their belts, lying by their bed curtains waiting for death.

sentences.zh: 千里絕煙，人跡罕見，白骨成聚，如丘隴焉。

translations.literal: For a thousand li smoke was gone and human tracks rarely seen; white bones heaped like mounds and hillocks.
translations.idiomatic: For a thousand li no smoke rose and human tracks were rare; white bones lay heaped like hills.

sentences.zh: 景性殘酷，於石頭立大碓，有犯法者搗殺之。

translations.literal: Jing's nature was cruel; at Shitou he set up a great pestle and killed lawbreakers by pounding.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing was cruel by nature. At Shitou he set up a great pestle and killed lawbreakers by pounding them to death.

sentences.zh: 常戒諸將曰：「破柵平城，當淨殺之，使天下知吾威名。

translations.literal: He often warned his generals: "When you break palisades and level cities, you should kill them clean, so all under Heaven knows my dread name.
translations.idiomatic: He often warned his generals: "When you break palisades and level cities, kill them clean, so all under Heaven knows my dread name.

sentences.zh: 」故諸將每戰勝，專以焚掠為事，斬刈人如草芥，以資戲笑。

translations.literal: " Therefore whenever his generals won battle they devoted themselves to burning and plunder, cutting men like grass for sport and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: " So whenever his generals won they devoted themselves to burning and plunder, cutting men like grass for sport and laughter.

sentences.zh: 由是百姓雖死，終不附之。

translations.literal: Because of this, though the common people died, in the end they would not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, though the people died in masses, in the end they would not follow him.

sentences.zh: 又禁人偶語，犯者刑及外族。

translations.literal: He also forbade people to speak in pairs; offenders' punishment reached their outer kin.
translations.idiomatic: He also forbade people to speak in pairs; offenders' kin were punished as well.

sentences.zh: 為其將帥者，悉稱行台，來降附者，悉稱開府，其親寄隆重者曰左右廂公，勇力兼人者曰庫直都督。

translations.literal: Those who were his generals all called themselves Mobile Headquarters; those who came to submit all called themselves Independent Staff; those he trusted most heavily were called Left and Right Wing Lords; those whose courage and strength matched many men were called Armory Direct Commanders.
translations.idiomatic: His generals all called themselves mobile headquarters; those who submitted called themselves independent staff; those he trusted most were left and right wing lords; men of matchless strength were armory direct commanders.

sentences.zh: 魏封皇子儒為燕王，公為吳王。

translations.literal: Wei enfeoffed the imperial prince Ru as Prince of Yan and Gong as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei enfeoffed imperial prince Ru as prince of Yan and Gong as prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 侯景召宋子仙還京口。

translations.literal: Hou Jing summoned Song Zixian back to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing summoned Song Zixian back to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸在郢州，以聽事為正陽殿，內外齋閣，悉加題署。

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling Lun was at Ying province; he made the audience hall into Zhengyang Palace and labeled all inner and outer fasting pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Shaoling was at Ying province. He turned the audience hall into Zhengyang Palace and labeled every inner and outer fasting pavilion.

sentences.zh: 其部下陵暴軍府，郢州將佐莫不怨之。

translations.literal: His subordinates bullied the army headquarters; Ying province officers none but resented it.
translations.idiomatic: His men bullied the army headquarters; every officer in Ying province resented it.

sentences.zh: 咨議參軍江仲舉，南平王恪之謀主也，說恪圖綸，恪驚曰：「若我殺邵陵，寧靜一鎮，荊、益兄弟必皆內喜，海內若平，則以大義責我矣。

translations.literal: Advisory Staff Officer Jiang Zhongju, chief strategist of Prince of Nanping Ke, urged Ke to plot against Lun; Ke in alarm said: "If I kill the Prince of Shaoling, I may quiet one province, but the brothers of Jing and Yi will all rejoice inwardly; if the realm is pacified, they will rebuke me with righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Advisory staff officer Jiang Zhongju, chief strategist of Prince Ke of Nanping, urged Ke to plot against Lun. Ke said in alarm: "If I kill the Prince of Shaoling I may quiet one province, but the princes of Jing and Yi will rejoice inwardly; if the realm is pacified they will rebuke me in the name of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 且巨逆未梟，骨肉相殘，自亡之道也。

translations.literal: Moreover the great rebel is not yet slain—kin slaughtering kin is the road to self-destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the great rebel is not yet slain—kin slaughtering kin is the road to ruin.

sentences.zh: 卿且息之。

translations.literal: Sir, cease this for now.
translations.idiomatic: Stop this for now.

sentences.zh: 」仲舉不從，部分諸將，刻日將發；

translations.literal: " Zhongju would not follow; he assigned the generals and set a day to launch;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongju would not listen. He assigned the generals and set a day to strike;

sentences.zh: 謀洩，綸壓殺之。

translations.literal: the plot leaked and Lun crushed and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: the plot leaked and Lun crushed and killed him.

sentences.zh: 恪狼狽往謝，綸曰：「群小所作，非由兄也。

translations.literal: Ke in distress went to apologize; Lun said: "Petty men did this—not through elder brother's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Ke went in distress to apologize. Lun said: "Petty men did this—not through your doing, elder brother.

sentences.zh: 凶黨已斃，兄勿深憂。

translations.literal: The evil faction is already dead; elder brother, do not grieve deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The plotters are dead. Do not grieve, elder brother.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯急攻長沙，辛巳，克之。

translations.literal: Wang Senbian pressed the attack on Changsha urgently; on xinsi, he took it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Senbian pressed the attack on Changsha. On xinsi he took it.

sentences.zh: 執河東王譽，斬之，傳首江陵，湘東王繹反其首而葬之。

translations.literal: He seized Prince of Hedong Yu, beheaded him, sent the head to Jiangling; Prince of Xiangdong Yi returned the head and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Prince Yu of Hedong, beheaded him, and sent the head to Jiangling. Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong returned the head and buried it.

sentences.zh: 初，世子方等之死，臨蒸周鐵虎功最多，譽委遇甚重。

translations.literal: Earlier, at Heir Fangdeng's death, Zhou Tiehu of Linzheng had done the most merit; Yu entrusted and favored him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when heir Fangdeng died, Zhou Tiehu of Linzheng had done the most. Yu trusted and favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 僧辯得鐵虎，命烹之，呼曰：「侯景未滅，奈何殺壯士！

translations.literal: Senbian captured Tiehu and ordered him boiled; Tiehu cried: "Hou Jing is not yet destroyed—how can you kill a brave man!
translations.idiomatic: Senbian captured Tiehu and ordered him boiled. Tiehu cried: "Hou Jing is not yet destroyed—how can you kill a brave man!

sentences.zh: 」僧辯奇其言而釋之，還其麾下。

translations.literal: " Senbian marveled at his words and released him, returning him to his command.
translations.idiomatic: " Senbian marveled at his words, released him, and returned him to his command.

sentences.zh: 繹以僧辯為左衛將軍，加侍中、鎮西長史。

translations.literal: Yi made Senbian Left Guard General, added Palace Attendant and Western Garrison Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yi made Senbian left guard general, added palace attendant and western garrison chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 繹自去歲聞高祖之喪，以長沙未下，故匿之。

translations.literal: Yi himself, since last year when he heard of Gaozu's death, because Changsha had not fallen, therefore concealed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi himself, since learning of Emperor Wu's death the year before, had concealed the news because Changsha had not yet fallen.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，始發喪，刻檀為高祖像，置於百福殿，事之甚謹，動靜必咨焉。

translations.literal: On renyin he at last announced the mourning, carved an image of Gaozu in sandalwood, placed it in Baifu Hall, served it with great reverence, and in movement or rest always consulted it.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he at last announced the mourning, carved a sandalwood image of Emperor Wu, placed it in Baifu Hall, and served it with such reverence that in every move he consulted it.

sentences.zh: 繹以為天子制於賊臣，不肯從大寶之號，猶稱太清四年。

translations.literal: Yi held that the Son of Heaven was controlled by rebel ministers and would not follow the Dabao era name, still calling it the fourth year of Taiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi held that the Son of Heaven was controlled by rebel ministers and would not adopt the Dabao era name, still calling it the fourth year of Taiqing.

sentences.zh: 丙午，繹下令大舉討侯景，移檄遠近。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Yi ordered a great campaign against Hou Jing and sent proclamations to far and near.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Yi ordered a great campaign against Hou Jing and sent proclamations far and near.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王范至湓城，以晉熙為晉州，遣其世子嗣為刺史，江州郡縣多輒改易。

translations.literal: Prince of Poyang Fan reached Pencheng, made Jinxi into Jin province, sent his heir Si as inspector; many Jiangzhou commanderies and counties were changed at will.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fan of Poyang reached Pencheng, made Jinxi into Jin province, and sent his heir Si as inspector; many Jiangzhou counties were changed at will.

sentences.zh: 尋陽王大心，政令所行，不出一郡。

translations.literal: Prince Daxin of Xunyang—his government's orders reached no farther than one commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daxin of Xunyang—his orders reached no farther than one commandery.

sentences.zh: 大心遣兵擊莊鐵，嗣與鐵素善，請發兵救之，范遣侯瑱帥精甲五千助鐵。

translations.literal: Daxin sent troops against Zhuang Tie; Si and Tie had long been friendly and asked that troops be sent to rescue; Fan sent Hou Zhen leading five thousand elite armored men to aid Tie.
translations.idiomatic: Daxin sent troops against Zhuang Tie. Si and Tie had long been friends and asked for rescue; Fan sent Hou Zhen with five thousand elite armored men to aid Tie.

sentences.zh: 由是二鎮互相猜忌，無復討賊之志。

translations.literal: Because of this the two garrisons mutually suspected one another and had no further will to campaign against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: From this the two garrisons grew mutually suspicious and lost all will to fight the rebels.

sentences.zh: 大心使徐嗣徽帥眾二千，築壘稽亭以備范，市糴不通，范數萬之眾，無所得食，多餓死。

translations.literal: Daxin had Xu Sihui lead two thousand men to build a fort at Jiting to guard against Fan; market grain could not pass; Fan's force of tens of thousands got no food and many starved.
translations.idiomatic: Daxin had Xu Sihui lead two thousand men to build a fort at Jiting against Fan. Grain could not reach the markets; Fan's army of tens of thousands found no food and many starved.

sentences.zh: 范憤恚，疽發於背，五月，乙卯，卒。

translations.literal: Fan, angry and resentful, had a carbuncle break out on his back; in the fifth month, on yimao, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, furious and resentful, developed a carbuncle on his back. In the fifth month, on yimao, he died.

sentences.zh: 其眾秘不發喪，奉范弟安南侯恬為主，有眾數千人。

translations.literal: His troops secretly did not announce the mourning and made Fan's younger brother Marquis Tian of Annan their leader, with several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: His troops kept the death secret and made Fan's younger brother Marquis Tian of Annan their leader, with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，侯景以元思虔為東道大行台，鎮錢塘。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Hou Jing made Yuan Siqian Eastern Route Grand Mobile Headquarters, garrisoning Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Hou Jing made Yuan Siqian eastern route grand mobile headquarters and garrisoned him at Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以侯子鑒為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingsi, he made Hou Zijian Southern Yanzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, he made Hou Zijian Southern Yanzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 東魏齊王洋之為開府也，勃海高德政為管記，由是親暱，言無不盡。

translations.literal: When Eastern Wei's Prince of Qi Yang was made Independent Staff, Gao Dezheng of Bohai was his chief clerk; from this they were intimate and spoke without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yang, prince of Qi in Eastern Wei, opened an independent staff, Gao Dezheng of Bohai was his chief clerk; from this they were intimate and spoke without reserve.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫丹楊徐之才、北平太守廣宗宋景業，皆善圖讖，以為太歲在午，當有革命，因德政以白洋，勸之受禪。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Brightness Xu Zhicai of Danyang and Beiping Administrator Song Jingye of Guangzong were both skilled in prognostic texts and held that with the Grand Year in wu there must be revolution; through Dezheng they informed Yang and urged him to accept the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Grand master of splendid brightness Xu Zhicai of Danyang and Beiping administrator Song Jingye of Guangzong were both skilled in prognostic texts. They held that with the Grand Year in wu there must be revolution; through Dezheng they told Yang and urged him to accept the throne.

sentences.zh: 洋以告婁太妃，太妃曰：「汝父如龍，兄如虎，猶以天位不可妄據，終身北面。

translations.literal: Yang told Grand Consort Lou; the Grand Consort said: "Your father was like a dragon, your elder brother like a tiger, yet they still held that Heaven's throne must not be seized rashly and faced north all their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Yang told Grand Consort Lou. She said: "Your father was like a dragon, your brother like a tiger, yet they held that Heaven's throne must not be seized rashly and faced north all their lives.

sentences.zh: 汝獨何人，欲行舜、禹之事乎！

translations.literal: Who are you alone, that you wish to do what Shun and Yu did!
translations.idiomatic: Who are you, that you wish to do what Shun and Yu did!

sentences.zh: 」洋以告之才，之才曰：「正為不及父兄，故宜早升尊位耳。

translations.literal: " Yang told Zhicai; Zhicai said: "It is precisely because you do not match father and elder brother that you should early ascend the honored throne.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang told Zhicai. Zhicai said: "It is precisely because you do not match your father and brother that you should ascend the throne early.

sentences.zh: 」洋鑄像卜之而成，乃使開府儀同三司段韶問肆州刺史斛律金，金來見洋，固言不可，以宋景業首陳符命，請殺之。

translations.literal: " Yang cast an image and divined; it succeeded; he then sent Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes Duan Shao to ask Sizhou Inspector Hulu Jin; Jin came to see Yang and firmly said it could not be done; he cited Song Jingye as first to proclaim the mandate and asked to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang cast an image and divined successfully. He sent equal in honor to the three dukes Duan Shao to ask Sizhou inspector Hulu Jin. Jin came, firmly opposed the plan, named Song Jingye as first to proclaim the mandate, and asked to kill him.

sentences.zh: 洋與諸貴議於太妃前，太妃曰：「吾兒懦直，必無此心，高德政樂禍，教之耳。

translations.literal: Yang discussed with the nobles before the Grand Consort; the Grand Consort said: "My son is timid and straight; he surely has no such heart—Gao Dezheng delights in disaster and taught him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang discussed with the nobles before the Grand Consort. She said: "My son is timid and straight; he surely has no such heart. Gao Dezheng delights in disaster and taught him.

sentences.zh: 」洋以人心不壹，使高德政如鄴察公卿之意，未還；

translations.literal: " Yang, because men's hearts were not united, sent Gao Dezheng to Ye to observe the intent of the dukes and ministers; he had not returned;
translations.idiomatic: " Because hearts were not united, Yang sent Gao Dezheng to Ye to sound out the dukes and ministers. He had not returned;

sentences.zh: 洋擁兵而東，至平都城，召諸勳貴議之，莫敢對。

translations.literal: Yang led troops east, reached Pingdu city, summoned the meritorious nobles to discuss it, and none dared answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yang led troops east to Pingdu city, summoned the meritorious nobles to discuss it, and none dared answer.

sentences.zh: 長史杜弼曰：「關西，國之勁敵，若受魏禪，恐彼挾天子，自稱義兵而東向，王何以待之！

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Du Bi said: "Guanxi is the state's fierce enemy; if you accept Wei's abdication, I fear they will hold the Son of Heaven and call themselves a righteous army marching east—how will my lord meet them!
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Du Bi said: "Guanxi is the state's fierce enemy. If you accept Wei's abdication, I fear they will hold the Son of Heaven, call themselves a righteous army, and march east—how will you meet them!

sentences.zh: 」徐之才曰：「今與王爭天下者，彼亦欲為王所為。

translations.literal: " Xu Zhicai said: "Those who contend with my lord for the realm today also wish to do what my lord does.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Zhicai said: "Those who contend with you for the realm today also wish to do what you do.

sentences.zh: 縱其屈強，不過隨我稱帝耳。

translations.literal: Even if they are stubborn and strong, at most they will follow us in calling themselves emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they are stubborn, at most they will follow us in calling themselves emperor.

sentences.zh: 」弼無以應。

translations.literal: " Bi had nothing to answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi had nothing to answer.

sentences.zh: 高德政至鄴，諷公卿，莫有應者。

translations.literal: Gao Dezheng reached Ye and hinted to the dukes and ministers; none responded.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dezheng reached Ye and sounded out the dukes and ministers; none responded.

sentences.zh: 司馬子如逆洋於遼陽，固言未可。

translations.literal: Sima Ziru met Yang at Liaoyang and firmly said it could not yet be done.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ziru met Yang at Liaoyang and firmly said it could not yet be done.

sentences.zh: 洋欲還，倉丞李集曰：「王來為何事，而今欲還？

translations.literal: Yang wished to return; warehouse clerk Li Ji said: "My lord came for what affair, and now wishes to return?
translations.idiomatic: Yang wished to return. Warehouse clerk Li Ji said: "My lord came for what affair, and now wishes to return?

sentences.zh: 」洋偽使於東門殺之，而別令賜絹十匹，遂還晉陽，自是居常不悅。

translations.literal: " Yang falsely had him killed at the east gate, then separately ordered ten bolts of silk given; he then returned to Jinyang and from this was usually unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang had him killed at the east gate on a pretext, then separately ordered ten bolts of silk given as gift. He returned to Jinyang and from then on was usually unhappy.

sentences.zh: 徐之才、宋景業等日陳陰陽雜占，雲宜早受命。

translations.literal: Xu Zhicai, Song Jingye, and others daily set forth yin-yang and miscellaneous divinations, saying he should early receive the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhicai, Song Jingye, and others daily urged yin-yang divinations, saying he should receive the mandate early.

sentences.zh: 高德政亦敦勸不已。

translations.literal: Gao Dezheng also pressed him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dezheng also pressed him without cease.

sentences.zh: 洋使術士李密卜之，遇《大橫》，曰：「漢文之卦也。

translations.literal: Yang had diviner Li Mi divine for him; he met Great Horizontal and said: "It is Emperor Wen of Han's hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: Yang had diviner Li Mi cast the hexagrams. He met Great Horizontal and said: "It is Emperor Wen of Han's hexagram.

sentences.zh: 」又使宋景業筮之，遇《乾》之《鼎》，曰：「《乾》，君也。

translations.literal: " He again had Song Jingye perform milfoil divination; he met Qian changing to Ding and said: "Qian is the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: " He again had Song Jingye perform milfoil divination. He met Qian changing to Ding and said: "Qian is the ruler.

sentences.zh: 《鼎》，五月卦也。

translations.literal: Ding is the fifth-month hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: Ding is the fifth-month hexagram.

sentences.zh: 宜以仲夏受禪。

translations.literal: You should receive the abdication in midsummer.
translations.idiomatic: You should receive the abdication in midsummer.

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「五月不可入官，犯之，終於其位。

translations.literal: " Someone said: "The fifth month is not fit to enter office; if you violate this, you will end in your post.
translations.idiomatic: " Someone said: "The fifth month is not fit to enter office; violate that taboo and you will end in your post.

sentences.zh: 」景業曰：「王為天子，無復下期，豈得不終於其位乎！

translations.literal: " Jingye said: "When my lord is Son of Heaven there is no next term—how can you not end in your post!
translations.idiomatic: " Jingye said: "When you are Son of Heaven there is no next term—how can you not end in your post!

sentences.zh: 」洋大悅，乃發晉陽。

translations.literal: " Yang was greatly pleased and then set out from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang was greatly pleased and set out from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 高德政錄在鄴諸事，條進於洋，洋令左右陳山提馳驛繼事條並密書與楊愔。

translations.literal: Gao Dezheng recorded all affairs at Ye and submitted them item by item to Yang; Yang ordered his attendant Chen Shanti to gallop post-horses with the continued item lists and a secret letter to Yang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dezheng recorded all affairs at Ye and submitted them item by item to Yang. Yang ordered his attendant Chen Shanti to gallop post-horses with the continued lists and a secret letter to Yang Yin.

sentences.zh: 是月，山提至鄴，楊愔即召太常卿邢劭等議撰儀注，秘書監魏收草九錫、禪讓、勸進諸文；

translations.literal: That month Shanti reached Ye; Yang Yin at once summoned Minister of Ceremonies Xing Shao and others to discuss drafting ritual protocols; Secretariat Director Wei Shou drafted the texts for the Nine Bestowals, abdication, and urging to advance;
translations.idiomatic: That month Shanti reached Ye. Yang Yin at once summoned minister of ceremonies Xing Shao and others to draft ritual protocols; secretariat director Wei Shou drafted the texts for the nine bestowals, abdication, and urging to advance;

sentences.zh: 引魏宗室諸王入北宮，留於東齋。

translations.literal: he brought in the various princes of the Wei imperial house to the Northern Palace and detained them in the Eastern Study.
translations.idiomatic: he brought the Wei imperial princes into the Northern Palace and detained them in the Eastern Study.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，東魏進洋位相國，總百揆，備九錫。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Eastern Wei advanced Yang to Chancellor, overall director of the hundred affairs, with the full Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Eastern Wei advanced Yang to chancellor, overall director of the hundred affairs, with the full nine bestowals.

sentences.zh: 洋行至前亭，所乘馬忽倒，意甚惡之。

translations.literal: As Yang traveled he reached Front Pavilion; the horse he rode suddenly fell and he took it as a very ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: As Yang traveled he reached Front Pavilion. His horse suddenly fell and he took it as a very ill omen.

sentences.zh: 至平都城，不復肯進。

translations.literal: Reaching Pingdu city, he would advance no farther.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Pingdu city, he would advance no farther.

sentences.zh: 高德政、徐之才苦請曰：「山提先去，恐其漏洩。

translations.literal: Gao Dezheng and Xu Zhicai urgently pleaded: "Shanti went ahead first—we fear he will leak the secret.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dezheng and Xu Zhicai urgently pleaded: "Shanti went ahead first—we fear he will leak the secret.

sentences.zh: 」即命司馬子如、杜弼馳驛續入，觀察物情。

translations.literal: " He at once ordered Sima Ziru and Du Bi to gallop post-horses in continued entry to observe how affairs stood.
translations.idiomatic: " He at once ordered Sima Ziru and Du Bi to gallop post-horses after them to observe how affairs stood.

sentences.zh: 子如等至鄴，眾人以事勢已決，無敢異言。

translations.literal: When Ziru and the rest reached Ye, the crowd, seeing the matter already decided, dared no dissenting word.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziru and the rest reached Ye, seeing the matter already decided, the crowd dared no dissenting word.

sentences.zh: 洋至鄴，召夫繼築具集城南。

translations.literal: When Yang reached Ye, he summoned laborers to continue building implements gathered south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang reached Ye, he summoned laborers to continue building the ritual implements gathered south of the city.

sentences.zh: 高隆之請曰：「用此何為？

translations.literal: Gao Longzhi asked: "What is this for?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Longzhi asked: "What is this for?

sentences.zh: 」洋作色曰：「我自有事，君何問為！

translations.literal: " Yang changed color and said: "I have my own affair—why do you ask!
translations.idiomatic: " Yang changed color and said: "I have my own affair—why do you ask!

sentences.zh: 欲族滅邪！

translations.literal: Do you wish your clan destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: Do you wish your clan destroyed!

sentences.zh: 」隆之謝而退。

translations.literal: " Longzhi apologized and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Longzhi apologized and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是作圜丘，備法物。

translations.literal: Thereupon they made the Round Mound Altar and prepared ritual implements.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they made the Round Mound Altar and prepared ritual implements.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，司空潘樂、侍中張亮、黃門郎趙彥深等求入啟事，東魏孝靜帝在昭陽殿見之。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Minister of Works Pan Yue, Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Liang, Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhao Yanshen, and others asked to enter with reports; Eastern Wei's Emperor Xiaojing received them in Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, minister of works Pan Yue, attendant-in-ordinary Zhang Liang, yellow gate gentleman Zhao Yanshen, and others asked to enter with reports. Eastern Wei's Emperor Xiaojing received them in Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「五行遞運，有始有終。

translations.literal: Liang said: "The Five Phases pass in turn; there is beginning and there is end.
translations.idiomatic: Liang said: "The Five Phases pass in turn; there is beginning and there is end.

sentences.zh: 齊王聖德欽明，萬方歸仰，願陛下遠法堯、舜。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi's sacred virtue is revered and bright; the ten thousand regions turn to him—may Your Majesty follow Yao and Shun from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Qi's sacred virtue is revered and bright; the ten thousand regions turn to him—may Your Majesty follow Yao and Shun from afar.

sentences.zh: 」帝斂容曰：「此事推挹已久，謹當遜避。

translations.literal: " The emperor composed his face and said: "This matter has been deferred long; I shall respectfully yield and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor composed his face and said: "This matter has been deferred long; I shall respectfully yield and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「若爾，須作制書。

translations.literal: " He also said: "If so, an imperial order must be drafted.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said: "If so, an imperial order must be drafted.

sentences.zh: 」中書郎崔劼、裴讓之曰：「制已作訖。

translations.literal: " Secretariat Gentlemen Cui Jie and Pei Rangzhi said: "The order is already drafted.
translations.idiomatic: " Secretariat gentlemen Cui Jie and Pei Rangzhi said: "The order is already drafted.

sentences.zh: 」使侍中楊愔進之。

translations.literal: " He had Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Yin present it.
translations.idiomatic: " He had attendant-in-ordinary Yang Yin present it.

sentences.zh: 東魏主既署，曰：「居朕何所？

translations.literal: After the Eastern Wei ruler had signed, he said: "Where shall I dwell?
translations.idiomatic: After the Eastern Wei ruler had signed, he said: "Where shall I dwell?

sentences.zh: 」愔對曰：「北城別有館宇。

translations.literal: " Yin answered: "The northern city has separate lodgings.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin answered: "The northern city has separate lodgings.

sentences.zh: 」乃下御坐，步就東廊，詠范蔚宗《後漢書‧贊》曰：「獻坐不辰，身播國屯，終我四百，永作虞賓。

translations.literal: " He then descended the imperial seat, walked to the eastern corridor, and recited Fan Ye's "Praise" in the Book of Later Han: "The Offered Emperor sat out of season, his person cast about in the state's hardship; he ended our four hundred years, forever to be the guest of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: " He descended the imperial seat, walked to the eastern corridor, and recited Fan Ye's praise in the Book of Later Han: "The offered emperor sat out of season, his person cast about in the state's hardship; he ended our four hundred years, forever to be the guest of Yu.

sentences.zh: 」所司請發，帝曰：「古人念遺簪弊履，朕欲與六宮別，可乎？

translations.literal: " The responsible office asked to depart; the emperor said: "The ancients treasured even lost hairpins and worn shoes—may I take leave of the six palaces?
translations.idiomatic: " The responsible office asked to depart. The emperor said: "The ancients treasured even lost hairpins and worn shoes—may I take leave of the six palaces?

sentences.zh: 」高隆之曰：「今日天下猶陛下之天下，況在六宮！

translations.literal: " Gao Longzhi said: "Today the realm is still Your Majesty's realm—how much more the six palaces!
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Longzhi said: "Today the realm is still Your Majesty's realm—how much more the six palaces!

sentences.zh: 」帝步入，與妃嬪已下別，舉宮皆哭。

translations.literal: " The emperor walked in and took leave of consorts and below; the whole palace wept.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor walked in and took leave of consorts and attendants; the whole palace wept.

sentences.zh: 趙國李嬪誦陳思王詩云：「王其愛玉體，俱享黃發期。

translations.literal: Lady Li of Zhao recited Prince Si of Chen's poem: "My lord, cherish your jade body and together enjoy the yellow-hair years.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li of Zhao recited Prince Si of Chen's poem: "My lord, cherish your jade body and together enjoy the years of gray hair.

sentences.zh: 」直長趙道德以故犢車一乘候於東閣，帝登車，道德超上抱之，帝叱之曰：「朕自畏天順人，何物奴敢逼人如此！

translations.literal: " Direct Attendant Zhao Daode waited at the eastern gate with one old ox-cart; the emperor mounted the cart; Daode sprang up and embraced him; the emperor shouted: "I myself fear Heaven and follow the people—what low slave dares press a man like this!
translations.idiomatic: " Direct attendant Zhao Daode waited at the eastern gate with one old ox-cart. The emperor mounted; Daode sprang up and embraced him. The emperor shouted: "I myself fear Heaven and follow the people—what low slave dares press a man like this!

sentences.zh: 」道德猶不下。

translations.literal: " Daode still would not descend.
translations.idiomatic: " Daode still would not descend.

sentences.zh: 出雲龍門，王公百僚拜辭，高隆之灑泣。

translations.literal: He went out through Cloud Dragon Gate; princes, dukes, and the hundred officials bowed in farewell; Gao Longzhi wept freely.
translations.idiomatic: He went out through Cloud Dragon Gate. Princes, dukes, and the hundred officials bowed in farewell. Gao Longzhi wept freely.

sentences.zh: 遂入北城，居司馬子如南宅，遣太尉彭城王韶等奉璽綬，禪位於齊。

translations.literal: He then entered the northern city, dwelt in Sima Ziru's southern residence, and sent Grand Commandant Prince Shao of Pengcheng and others to present seal and sash and abdicate the throne to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the northern city, dwelt in Sima Ziru's southern residence, and sent grand commandant Prince Shao of Pengcheng and others to present seal and sash and abdicate the throne to Qi.

sentences.zh: 戊午，齊王即皇帝位於南郊，大赦，改元天保。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Prince of Qi took the imperial throne at the southern suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the prince of Qi took the imperial throne at the southern suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 自魏敬宗以來，百官絕祿，至是始復給之。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Jingzong of Wei, the hundred offices had had no salaries; only now were they restored.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Jingzong of Wei, officials had received no salaries; only now were they restored.

sentences.zh: 己未，封東魏主為中山王，待以不臣之禮。

translations.literal: On jiwei, he enfeoffed the Eastern Wei ruler as Prince of Zhongshan and treated him with the ceremony due one who is not a subject.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, he enfeoffed the Eastern Wei ruler as prince of Zhongshan and treated him with the ceremony due one who is not a subject.

sentences.zh: 追尊齊獻武王為獻武皇帝，廟號太祖，後改為高祖；

translations.literal: He posthumously honored Prince of Qi Xianwu as Emperor Xianwu, temple name Taizu, later changed to Gaozu;
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored Prince Xianwu of Qi as Emperor Xianwu, temple name Taizu, later changed to Gaozu;

sentences.zh: 文襄王為文襄皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxiang as Emperor Wenxiang, temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang as Emperor Wenxiang, temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，尊王太后婁氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: On xinyou, he honored Grand Consort Lou as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, he honored Grand Consort Lou as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，降魏朝封爵有差，其宣力霸朝及西、南投化者，不在降限。

translations.literal: On yichou, he reduced Wei-dynasty enfeoffments and ranks by degrees; those who had proclaimed strength for the hegemon court and those who had submitted from west and south were not within the reduction limit.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, he reduced Wei-dynasty enfeoffments and ranks by degrees; those who had served the hegemon court and those who had submitted from west and south were exempt.

sentences.zh: 文成侯寧起兵於吳，有眾萬人，己巳，進攻吳郡；

translations.literal: Marquis Ning of Wencheng raised troops in Wu with ten thousand men; on jisi, he advanced to attack Wu commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Ning of Wencheng raised troops in Wu with ten thousand men. On jisi he advanced to attack Wu commandery;

sentences.zh: 行吳郡事侯子榮逆擊，殺之。

translations.literal: Acting Wu Administrator Hou Zirong struck back and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Wu administrator Hou Zirong struck back and killed him.

sentences.zh: 寧，范之弟也。

translations.literal: Ning was Fan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was Fan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 子榮因縱兵大掠郡境。

translations.literal: Zirong then let his troops plunder the commandery borders greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zirong then let his troops plunder the whole commandery.

sentences.zh: 自晉氏度江，三吳最為富庶，貢賦商旅，皆出其地。

translations.literal: Since the Jin house crossed the river, the Three Wu had been richest; tribute, taxes, merchants and travelers all came from that land.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin house crossed the river, the Three Wu had been richest; tribute, taxes, and merchants all flowed from that land.

sentences.zh: 及侯景之亂，掠金帛既盡，乃掠人而食之，或賣於北境，遺民殆盡矣。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing's rebellion came, after gold and silk were plundered clean they plundered men to eat them, or sold them to the northern borders; survivors were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing's rebellion came, after gold and silk were stripped bare they plundered men for food, or sold them to the northern borders; survivors were nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 是時，唯荊、益所部尚完實，太尉、益州刺史武陵王紀移告征、鎮，使世子圓照帥兵三萬受湘東王節度。

translations.literal: At this time only the parts held by Jing and Yi remained intact; Grand Commandant and Yizhou Inspector Prince Ji of Wuling sent notice to the campaign armies and garrisons, making his heir Yuanzhao lead thirty thousand men to accept Prince of Xiangdong Yi's command.
translations.idiomatic: At this time only the domains of Jing and Yi remained intact. Grand commandant and Yizhou inspector Prince Ji of Wuling sent notice to the campaign armies and garrisons, ordering his heir Yuanzhao to lead thirty thousand men under Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 圓照軍至巴水，繹授以信州刺史，令屯白帝，未許東下。

translations.literal: Yuanzhao's army reached Bashui; Yi made him Xinzhou Inspector and ordered him to camp at Baidi, not permitting him to go east.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhao's army reached the Bashui. Yi made him Xinzhou inspector, ordered him to camp at Baidi, and would not let him march east.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛巳，以南郡王大連行揚州事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinsi, Prince Dalian of Nan commandery was made acting Yangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinsi, Prince Dalian of Nan commandery was made acting Yangzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 江夏王大款、山陽王大成、宜都王大封自信安間道奔江陵。

translations.literal: Prince Dakuan of Jiangxia, Prince Dacheng of Shanyang, and Prince Dafeng of Yidu from Xin'an by hidden paths fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dakuan of Jiangxia, Prince Dacheng of Shanyang, and Prince Dafeng of Yidu fled from Xin'an by hidden paths to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 齊主封宗室高岳等十人、功臣庫狄乾等七人皆為王。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler enfeoffed ten clansmen including Gao Yue and seven meritorious ministers including Kudi Gan all as kings.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler enfeoffed ten clansmen including Gao Yue and seven meritorious ministers including Kudi Gan as kings.

sentences.zh: 癸未，封弟浚為永安王，淹為平陽王，浟為彭城王，演為常山王，渙為上黨王，淯為襄城王，湛為長廣王，湝為任城王，湜為高陽王，濟為博陵王，凝為新平王，潤為馮翊王，洽為漢陽王。

translations.literal: On guiwei, he enfeoffed his younger brothers Jun as Prince of Yong'an, Yan as Prince of Pingyang, You as Prince of Pengcheng, Yan as Prince of Changshan, Huan as Prince of Shangdang, Yu as Prince of Xiangcheng, Zhan as Prince of Changgang, Jie as Prince of Rencheng, Shi as Prince of Gaoyang, Ji as Prince of Boling, Ning as Prince of Xinping, Run as Prince of Fengyi, and Qia as Prince of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, he enfeoffed his younger brothers: Jun as prince of Yong'an, Yan as prince of Pingyang, You as prince of Pengcheng, Yan as prince of Changshan, Huan as prince of Shangdang, Yu as prince of Xiangcheng, Zhan as prince of Changgang, Jie as prince of Rencheng, Shi as prince of Gaoyang, Ji as prince of Boling, Ning as prince of Xinping, Run as prince of Fengyi, and Qia as prince of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王范既卒，侯瑱依莊鐵，鐵忌之；

translations.literal: After Prince of Poyang Fan had died, Hou Zhen relied on Zhuang Tie; Tie resented him;
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Fan of Poyang died, Hou Zhen relied on Zhuang Tie; Tie resented him;

sentences.zh: 瑱自安，丙戌，詐引鐵謀事，因殺之，自據豫章。

translations.literal: Zhen felt secure; on bingxu, he falsely summoned Tie to discuss plans and killed him, then seized Yuzhang for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen felt secure; on bingxu, he lured Zhuang Tie under pretense of counsel and killed him, then seized Yuzhang for himself.

sentences.zh: 尋陽王大心遣徐嗣徽夜襲湓城，安南侯恬、裴之橫等擊走之。

translations.literal: Prince Daxin of Xunyang sent Xu Sihui in a night raid on Pencheng; Marquis Tian of Annan, Pei Zhiheng, and others struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daxin of Xunyang sent Xu Sihui in a night raid on Pencheng; Marquis Tian of Annan, Pei Zhiheng, and others struck and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 齊主娶趙郡李希宗之女，生子殷及紹德；

translations.literal: The Qi emperor married the daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao commandery and had sons Yin and Shaode.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor married the daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao commandery and had sons Yin and Shaode.

sentences.zh: 又納段韶之妹。

translations.literal: He also took Duan Shao's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: He also took Duan Shao's younger sister as consort.

sentences.zh: 及將建中宮，高隆之、高德政欲結勳貴之援，乃言：「漢婦人不可為天下母，宜更擇美配。

translations.literal: When he was about to establish the empress, Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng wished to win support from meritorious nobles and said, "A Han woman cannot be mother to the realm; a finer match should be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to name an empress, Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng, seeking allies among the meritorious nobility, said, "A Han woman cannot be mother to the realm—a finer match should be chosen.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，立李氏為皇后，以段氏為昭儀，子殷為皇太子。

translations.literal: On dinghai, he made Lady Li empress, Lady Duan a Lady of Bright Deportment, and son Yin crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, he made Lady Li empress, Lady Duan a Lady of Bright Deportment, and son Yin crown prince.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以庫狄干為太宰，彭樂為太尉，潘相樂為司徒，司馬子如為司空。

translations.literal: On gengyin, he made Kudi Gan Grand Preceptor, Peng Yue Grand Commandant, Pan Xiangle Minister of Works, and Sima Ziru Minister of the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, he made Kudi Gan Grand Preceptor, Peng Yue Grand Commandant, Pan Xiangle Minister of Works, and Sima Ziru Minister of the Masses.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以清河王岳為司州牧。

translations.literal: On xinmao, he made Prince Yue of Qinghe Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, he made Prince Yue of Qinghe Governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 侯景以羊鴉仁為五兵尚書。

translations.literal: Hou Jing made Yang Yaren Minister of the Five Arms.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing made Yang Yaren Minister of the Five Arms.

sentences.zh: 庚子，鴉仁出奔江西，將赴江陵，至東莞，盜疑其懷金，邀殺之。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Yaren fled west of the river, intending to go to Jiangling; reaching Dongguan, bandits suspected he carried gold and waylaid and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Yaren fled west of the river toward Jiangling; at Dongguan, bandits suspected he carried gold and waylaid and killed him.

sentences.zh: 魏人欲令岳陽王察發哀嗣位，察辭，不受。

translations.literal: The Wei men wished Prince Cha of Yueyang to proclaim mourning and succeed to the throne; Cha declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei court wished Prince Cha of Yueyang to proclaim mourning and succeed to the throne; Cha declined.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰使榮權冊命察為梁王，始建台，置百官。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai sent Rong Quan with patent and mandate to enfeoff Cha as Prince of Liang; he first raised a headquarters and established the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yuwen Tai sent Rong Quan with patent and mandate to enfeoff Cha as Prince of Liang; Cha first raised a headquarters and established the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 陳霸先修崎頭古城，徙居之。

translations.literal: Chen Baxian repaired the old city at Qitou and moved his seat there.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baxian repaired the old city at Qitou and moved his seat there.

sentences.zh: 初，燕昭成帝奔高麗，使其族人馮業以三百人浮海奔宋，因留新會。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Zhaocheng of Yan fled to Goguryeo and had his clansman Feng Ye take three hundred men across the sea to flee to Song, and they remained at Xinhui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Zhaocheng of Yan fled to Goguryeo and sent his clansman Feng Ye with three hundred men across the sea to Song territory; they settled at Xinhui.

sentences.zh: 自業至孫融，世為羅州刺史，融子寶為高涼太守。

translations.literal: From Ye down to grandson Rong, the line served as Inspectors of Luozhou generation after generation; Rong's son Bao was Administrator of Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: From Ye down to grandson Rong, the line held Luozhou generation after generation; Rong's son Bao was administrator of Gaoliang.

sentences.zh: 高涼洗氏，世為蠻酋，部落十餘萬家，有女，多籌略，善用兵，諸洞皆服其信義；

translations.literal: The Xi clan of Gaoliang had for generations been chieftains among the barbarians, with more than a hundred thousand households in their tribes; they had a daughter of great stratagem who excelled at arms, and all the cave settlements trusted her integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi of Gaoliang had for generations been chieftains among the hill peoples, with more than a hundred thousand households in their tribes; they had a daughter of keen stratagem who excelled at arms, and every cave settlement trusted her word.

sentences.zh: 融聘以為寶婦。

translations.literal: Rong betrothed her to Bao as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Rong betrothed her to Bao as his wife.

sentences.zh: 融雖累世為方伯，非其土人，號令不行；

translations.literal: Though Rong had for generations been a frontier lord, he was not native to the soil and his orders did not take effect.
translations.idiomatic: Though Rong had for generations been a frontier lord, he was not native to the land and his orders did not take effect.

sentences.zh: 洗氏約束本宗，使從民禮，每與寶參決辭訟，首領有犯，雖親戚無所縱捨，由是馮氏始得行其政。

translations.literal: Lady Xi restrained her own clan, made them follow civil rites, joined Bao in judging lawsuits, and when chieftains offended showed no lenience even to kin; thereby the Feng line at last could enforce its rule.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xi restrained her own clan, made them follow civil law, joined Bao in judging lawsuits, and when chieftains offended showed no lenience even to kin—only then could the Feng line enforce its rule.

sentences.zh: 高州刺史李遷仕據大皋口，遣使召寶，寶欲往，洗氏止之曰：「刺史無故不應召太守，必欲詐君共反耳。

translations.literal: Gaozhou Inspector Li Qianshi held Dagao Pass and sent envoys summoning Bao; Bao wished to go; Lady Xi stopped him, saying, "An inspector should not summon an administrator without cause—he surely means to trick you into rebellion with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhou inspector Li Qianshi held Dagao Pass and summoned Bao; Bao wished to go; Lady Xi stopped him: "An inspector should not summon an administrator without cause—he surely means to trick you into rebellion with him.

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「何以知之？

translations.literal: " Bao said, "How do you know?
translations.idiomatic: " Bao said, "How do you know?

sentences.zh: 」洗氏曰：「刺史被召援台，乃稱有疾，鑄兵聚眾而後召君；

translations.literal: " Lady Xi said, "The inspector was summoned to aid the capital yet claims illness, casts weapons and gathers troops, and only then summons you.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Xi said, "The inspector was summoned to aid the capital yet claims illness, casts weapons and gathers troops, and only then summons you.

sentences.zh: 此必欲質君以發君之兵也，願且無往以觀其變。

translations.literal: He surely means to hold you hostage to raise your troops; I beg you not go yet and watch how matters turn.
translations.idiomatic: He surely means to hold you hostage to raise your troops; do not go yet—watch how matters turn.

sentences.zh: 」數日，遷仕果反，遣主帥杜平虜將兵入灨石，城魚梁以逼南康，陳霸先使周文育擊之。

translations.literal: " Within days Qianshi indeed rebelled, sent commander Du Pinglu with troops into Ganshi, walled Yuliang to press Nankang; Chen Baxian sent Zhou Wenyu to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: " Within days Qianshi rebelled, sent commander Du Pinglu into Ganshi, walled Yuliang to press Nankang; Chen Baxian sent Zhou Wenyu against him.

sentences.zh: 洗氏謂寶曰：「平虜，驍將也，今入贛石與官軍相拒，勢未得還，遷仕在州，無能為也。

translations.literal: Lady Xi told Bao, "Pinglu is a fierce general; now he has entered Ganshi to contend with the government army and cannot soon return; Qianshi in the province can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xi told Bao, "Pinglu is a fierce general; now he is locked in Ganshi against the government army and cannot soon return—Qianshi in the province is helpless.

sentences.zh: 君若自往，必有戰鬥，宜遣使卑辭厚禮告之曰：『身未敢出，欲遣婦參。

translations.literal: If you go yourself there will surely be battle; better send envoys with humble words and rich gifts, saying, 'I dare not come myself and wish to send my wife to attend.
translations.idiomatic: If you go yourself there will surely be battle; better send envoys with humble words and rich gifts, saying, 'I dare not come myself and wish to send my wife to attend.

sentences.zh: 』彼聞之，必喜而無備。

translations.literal: ' When he hears this he will be pleased and unguarded.
translations.idiomatic: ' When he hears that he will be pleased and drop his guard.

sentences.zh: 我將千餘人，步擔雜物，唱言輸賧，得至柵下，破之必矣。

translations.literal: I shall take more than a thousand men, carrying goods on foot, proclaiming tribute delivery; once we reach the palisade we shall surely break them.
translations.idiomatic: I shall take more than a thousand men on foot with bundled goods, proclaiming tribute delivery; once we reach the palisade we shall break them.

sentences.zh: 」寶從之。

translations.literal: " Bao followed her plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Bao followed her plan.

sentences.zh: 遷仕果不設備，洗氏襲擊，大破之，遷仕走保寧都。

translations.literal: Qianshi indeed made no preparations; Lady Xi struck by surprise and routed him; Qianshi fled to hold Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshi left himself unguarded; Lady Xi struck by surprise and routed him; Qianshi fled to hold Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 文育亦擊走平虜，據其城。

translations.literal: Wenyu also struck and drove off Pinglu and seized his city.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu also drove off Pinglu and seized his city.

sentences.zh: 洗氏與霸先會於灨石，還，謂寶曰：「陳都督非常人也，甚得眾心，必能平賊，君宜厚資之。

translations.literal: Lady Xi met Baxian at Ganshi; returning, she told Bao, "Commander Chen is no ordinary man; he wins men's hearts and will surely quell the rebels—you should support him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xi met Baxian at Ganshi; returning, she told Bao, "Commander Chen is no ordinary man; he wins men's hearts and will quell the rebels—you should support him generously.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹以霸先為豫州刺史，領豫章內史。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Xiangdong made Baxian Inspector of Yuzhou and concurrent Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong made Baxian Inspector of Yuzhou and concurrent Administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，裴之橫攻稽亭，徐嗣徽擊走之。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Pei Zhiheng attacked Jiting; Xu Sihui struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Pei Zhiheng attacked Jiting; Xu Sihui struck and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛亥，齊立世宗妃元氏為文襄皇后，宮曰靜德。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinhai, Qi established the Shizong consort of the Yuan clan as Empress Wenxiang, with palace name Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinhai, Qi established Shizong's consort of the Yuan clan as Empress Wenxiang, with palace name Jingde.

sentences.zh: 又封世宗子孝琬為河間王，孝瑜為河南王。

translations.literal: He also enfeoffed Shizong's sons Xiaowan as Prince of Hejian and Xiaoyu as Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He also enfeoffed Shizong's sons Xiaowan as Prince of Hejian and Xiaoyu as Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以尚書令封隆之錄尚書事，尚書左僕射平陽王淹為尚書令。

translations.literal: On yimao, he made Minister of Works Feng Longzhi Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing and Left Vice Minister of Works Prince Yan of Pingyang Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, he made Minister of Works Feng Longzhi Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing and Left Vice Minister Prince Yan of Pingyang Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，梁王察入朝於魏。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Prince of Liang Cha entered court in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Prince of Liang Cha entered court at the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 初，東魏遣儀同武威牒雲洛等迎鄱陽世子嗣，使鎮皖城。

translations.literal: Earlier, Eastern Wei sent Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes Wuwei Dieyun Luo and others to welcome Poyang Heir Si and station him at Wancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Eastern Wei sent Dieyun Luo of Wuwei, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and others to welcome Poyang heir Si and station him at Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 嗣未及行，任約軍至，洛等引去；

translations.literal: Si had not yet set out when Ren Yue's army arrived; Luo and the others withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Si had not yet set out when Ren Yue's army arrived; Luo and the others withdrew.

sentences.zh: 嗣遂失援，出戰，敗死。

translations.literal: Si thus lost support, went out to battle, was defeated, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Si thus lost support, went out to battle, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 約遂略地至湓城，尋陽王大心遣司馬韋質出戰而敗，帳下猶有戰士千餘人，鹹勸大心走保建州；

translations.literal: Yue then raided as far as Pencheng; Prince Daxin of Xunyang sent Chief Administrator Wei Zhi out to fight and was defeated; under his tent there remained more than a thousand fighting men, and all urged Daxin to flee and hold Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then raided as far as Pencheng; Prince Daxin of Xunyang sent chief administrator Wei Zhi out to fight and was defeated; more than a thousand warriors still stood under his tent, and all urged Daxin to flee and hold Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 大心不能用，戊辰，以江州降約。

translations.literal: Daxin would not follow them; on wuchen he surrendered Jiangzhou to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Daxin would not listen; on wuchen he surrendered Jiangzhou to Yue.

sentences.zh: 先是，大心使前太子洗馬韋臧鎮建昌，有甲士五千，聞尋陽不守，欲帥眾奔江陵，未發，為麾下所殺。

translations.literal: Earlier, Daxin had sent former Crown Prince Attendant Wei Zang to garrison Jianchang with five thousand armored men; hearing Xunyang had not held, he wished to lead his force to Jiangling; before he set out, his subordinates killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Daxin had sent former crown prince attendant Wei Zang to garrison Jianchang with five thousand armored men; hearing Xunyang had fallen, he wished to lead his force to Jiangling; before he could march, his own men killed him.

sentences.zh: 臧，粲之子也。

translations.literal: Zang was Can's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zang was Can's son.

sentences.zh: 於慶略地至豫章，侯瑱屈，降之，慶送瑱建康。

translations.literal: Yu Qing raided as far as Yuzhang; Hou Zhen submitted and surrendered; Qing sent Zhen to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qing raided as far as Yuzhang; Hou Zhen submitted; Qing sent Zhen to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 景以瑱姓，待之甚厚，留其妻子及弟為質，遣瑱慶徇蠡南諸郡，以瑱湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Jing, because of Zhen's surname, treated him very generously, kept his wife, children, and younger brother as hostages, sent Zhen with Qing to overrun the southern counties of Li, and made Zhen Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing, because of Zhen's surname, treated him generously, kept his wife, children, and younger brother as hostages, sent Zhen with Qing to overrun the southern counties of Li, and made Zhen Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，巴山人黃法□，有勇力，侯景之亂，合徒眾保鄉里。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huang Fa□ of Bashan, brave and strong, during Hou Jing's rebellion gathered followers to protect his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Huang Fa□ of Bashan, brave and strong, during Hou Jing's rebellion gathered followers to protect his home district.

sentences.zh: 太守賀詡下江州，命法□監郡事。

translations.literal: Administrator He Xu went down to Jiangzhou and ordered Fa□ to oversee commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator He Xu went down to Jiangzhou and ordered Fa□ to oversee commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 法□屯新淦，於慶自豫章分兵襲新水金，法□敗之。

translations.literal: Fa□ encamped at Xingan; Yu Qing from Yuzhang divided his force to raid Xinshuijin; Fa□ defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Fa□ encamped at Xingan; Yu Qing from Yuzhang divided his force to raid Xinshuijin; Fa□ defeated him.
