sentences.zh: 陳霸先使周文育進軍擊慶，法□引兵會之。

translations.literal: Chen Baxian sent Zhou Wenyu advancing to strike Qing; Fa□ led troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baxian sent Zhou Wenyu to strike Qing; Fa□ led troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸聞任約將至，使司馬蔣思安將精兵五千襲之，約眾潰；

translations.literal: Prince Lun of Shaoling heard Ren Yue was coming, sent Chief Administrator Jiang Si'an with five thousand elite troops to surprise him; Yue's force collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Shaoling heard Ren Yue was coming and sent chief administrator Jiang Si'an with five thousand elite troops to surprise him; Yue's force collapsed.

sentences.zh: 思安不設備，約收兵襲之，思安敗走。

translations.literal: Si'an made no preparations; Yue gathered his troops and struck him; Si'an was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Si'an left himself unguarded; Yue rallied his men and struck back; Si'an was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹改宜都為宜州，以王琳為刺史。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Xiangdong changed Yidu to Yizhou and made Wang Lin its inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong changed Yidu to Yizhou and made Wang Lin its inspector.

sentences.zh: 是月，以南郡王大連為江州刺史。

translations.literal: That month he made Prince Dalian of Nanjun Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That month he made Prince Dalian of Nanjun Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相泰以齊主稱帝，帥諸軍討之。

translations.literal: Wei Chancellor Tai, because the Qi emperor had claimed the throne, led the armies to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yuwen Tai, because the Qi emperor had claimed the throne, led the armies against him.

sentences.zh: 以齊王郭鎮隴右，征秦州刺史宇文導為大將軍、都督二十三州諸軍事，屯咸陽，鎮關中。

translations.literal: He made Prince Guo of Qi garrison Longyou, summoned Qinzhou Inspector Yuwen Dao as Grand General and Commander of Military Affairs in Twenty-three Provinces, encamped at Xianyang, and garrisoned Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He made Prince Guo of Qi garrison Longyou, summoned Qinzhou inspector Yuwen Dao as Grand General and Commander of Military Affairs in Twenty-three Provinces, encamped at Xianyang, and held Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 益州沙門孫天英帥徒數千人夜攻州城，武陵王紀與戰，斬之。

translations.literal: The monk Sun Tianying of Yizhou led several thousand followers in a night attack on the provincial city; Prince Ji of Wuling fought him and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Sun Tianying of Yizhou led several thousand followers in a night attack on the provincial city; Prince Ji of Wuling fought him and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸大修鎧仗，將討侯景。

translations.literal: Prince Lun of Shaoling greatly repaired armor and weapons, intending to attack Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Shaoling greatly repaired armor and weapons, intending to attack Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹惡之，八月，甲午，遣左衛將軍王僧辯、信州刺史鮑泉等帥舟師一萬東趣江、郢，聲言拒任約，且雲迎邵陵王還江陵，授以湘州。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Xiangdong resented this; in the eighth month, on jiawu, he sent Left Guard General Wang Senbian, Xinzhou Inspector Bao Quan, and others leading ten thousand men in ships east toward Jiang and Ying, proclaiming resistance to Ren Yue while also saying he would welcome Prince Lun back to Jiangling and grant him Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong resented this; in the eighth month, on jiawu, he sent Left Guard General Wang Senbian, Xinzhou inspector Bao Quan, and others with ten thousand men in ships east toward Jiang and Ying, proclaiming resistance to Ren Yue while also saying he would welcome Prince Lun back to Jiangling and grant him Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊主初立，勵精為治。

translations.literal: When the Qi emperor first took the throne, he strove diligently in government.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi emperor first took the throne, he strove diligently in government.

sentences.zh: 趙道德以事屬黎陽太守清河房超，超不發書，棓殺其使；

translations.literal: Zhao Daode entrusted a matter to Liyang Administrator Fang Chao of Qinghe; Chao would not release the document and clubbed his messenger to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Daode entrusted a matter to Liyang administrator Fang Chao of Qinghe; Chao would not release the document and clubbed his messenger to death.

sentences.zh: 齊主善之，命守宰各設棓以誅屬請之使。

translations.literal: The Qi emperor approved this and ordered every prefect and magistrate to set up clubs to execute messengers making improper requests.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor approved and ordered every prefect and magistrate to keep clubs at hand to execute messengers making improper requests.

sentences.zh: 久之，都官中郎宋軌奏曰：「若受使請賕，猶致大戮，身為枉法，何以加罪！

translations.literal: After long time, Palace Attendant of the Capital Bureau Song Gui memorialized, saying, "If accepting bribes through messengers still brings death, how can one add punishment for bending the law oneself!
translations.idiomatic: After long time, palace attendant Song Gui of the Capital Bureau memorialized: "If accepting bribes through messengers still brings death, how can one add punishment for bending the law oneself!

sentences.zh: 」乃罷之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the practice was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 司都功曹張老上書請定齊律，詔右僕射薛琡等取魏《麟趾格》，更討論損益之。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhang Lao of the Capital Bureau submitted a memorial asking to fix Qi law; an edict ordered Right Vice Minister Xue Ju and others to take Wei's Linzhi Code and revise it through discussion of what to add or cut.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Zhang Lao of the Capital Bureau asked that Qi law be fixed; an edict ordered Right Vice Minister Xue Ju and others to take Wei's Linzhi Code and revise it through discussion of what to add or cut.

sentences.zh: 齊主簡練六坊之人，每一人必當百人，任其臨陳必死，然後取之，謂之「百保鮮卑」。

translations.literal: The Qi emperor selected and trained men of the six wards so that each one must equal a hundred, taking only those who would surely die facing battle, and called them the "Hundred-Guard Xianbei."
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor selected men of the six wards so that each must equal a hundred, taking only those who would die facing battle without flinching, and called them the "Hundred-Guard Xianbei."

sentences.zh: 又簡華人之勇力絕倫者，謂之「勇士」，以備邊要。

translations.literal: He also selected Chinese of unmatched courage and strength, called them "Warriors," to guard critical frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: He also selected Chinese of unmatched courage and strength, called them "Warriors," to guard critical frontiers.

sentences.zh: 始立九等之戶，富者稅其錢，貧者役其力。

translations.literal: He first established nine grades of households: the rich were taxed in coin, the poor in labor.
translations.idiomatic: He first established nine grades of households: the rich were taxed in coin, the poor in labor.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁巳，魏軍發長安。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingsi, the Wei army set out from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingsi, the Wei army set out from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯軍至鸚鵡洲，郢州司馬劉龍虎等潛送質於僧辯，邵陵王綸聞之，遣其子威正侯礩將兵擊之，龍虎敗，奔於僧辯。

translations.literal: Wang Senbian's army reached Parrot Islet; Yingzhou Chief Administrator Liu Longhu and others secretly sent hostages to Senbian; Prince Lun of Shaoling heard of it and sent his son Marquis Li of Weizheng with troops to strike them; Longhu was defeated and fled to Senbian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Senbian's army reached Parrot Islet; Yingzhou chief administrator Liu Longhu and others secretly sent hostages to Senbian; Prince Lun of Shaoling heard and sent his son Marquis Li of Weizheng to strike them; Longhu was defeated and fled to Senbian.

sentences.zh: 綸以書責僧辯曰：「將軍前年殺人之侄，今歲伐人之兄，以此求榮，恐天下不許！

translations.literal: Lun wrote Senbian a letter of reproach, saying, "General, last year you killed a man's nephew; this year you attack a man's elder brother—with this you seek glory, and I fear the realm will not allow it!
translations.idiomatic: Lun wrote Senbian a letter of reproach: "General, last year you killed a man's nephew; this year you attack a man's elder brother—with this you seek glory, and I fear the realm will not allow it!

sentences.zh: 」僧辯送書於湘東王繹，繹命進軍。

translations.literal: " Senbian forwarded the letter to Prince Yi of Xiangdong; Yi ordered the advance.
translations.idiomatic: " Senbian forwarded the letter to Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong; Yi ordered the advance.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，綸集其麾下於西園，涕泣言曰：「我本無他，志在滅賊，湘東常謂與之爭帝，遂爾見伐。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Lun gathered his followers in the Western Garden and said through tears, "I had no other aim but to destroy the rebels; Xiangdong always believed I contended with him for the throne, and so I am attacked.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Lun gathered his followers in the Western Garden and said through tears, "I had no other aim but to destroy the rebels; Xiangdong always believed I contended with him for the throne, and so I am attacked.

sentences.zh: 今日欲守則交絕糧儲，欲戰則取笑千載，不容無事受縛，當於下流避之。

translations.literal: Today, to hold fast cuts off grain and stores; to fight invites mockery for a thousand years; I cannot accept binding without cause—I shall withdraw downriver.
translations.idiomatic: Today, to hold fast cuts off grain and stores; to fight invites mockery for a thousand years; I cannot accept binding without cause—I shall withdraw downriver.

sentences.zh: 」麾下壯士爭請出戰，綸不從，與礩自倉門登舟北出。

translations.literal: " His stalwart followers all begged to fight; Lun would not agree and boarded a boat with Li through the granary gate and went north.
translations.idiomatic: " His stalwart followers all begged to fight; Lun would not agree and boarded a boat with Li through the granary gate and went north.

sentences.zh: 僧辯入據郢州。

translations.literal: Senbian entered and seized Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian entered and seized Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 繹以南平王恪為尚書令、開府儀同三司，世子方諸為郢州刺史，王僧辯為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Yi made Prince Ke of Nanping Minister of Works and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an Opening Office, Heir Fangzhu Inspector of Yingzhou, and Wang Senbian General of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yi made Prince Ke of Nanping Minister of Works and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an Opening Office, heir Fangzhu inspector of Yingzhou, and Wang Senbian General of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 綸遇鎮東將軍裴之高於道，之高之子畿掠其軍器，綸與左右輕舟奔武昌澗飲寺，僧法馨匿綸於巖穴之下。

translations.literal: Lun met Garrison-East General Pei Zhigao on the road; Zhigao's son Ji plundered his military gear; Lun with his close followers fled in light boats to Wuchang's Jianyin Temple, where the monk Favin hid Lun in a cave below the cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: Lun met garrison-east general Pei Zhigao on the road; Zhigao's son Ji plundered his military gear; Lun with his close followers fled in light boats to Wuchang's Jianyin Temple, where the monk Favin hid him in a cave below the cliffs.

sentences.zh: 綸長史韋質、司馬姜律等聞綸尚存，馳往迎之，說七柵流民以求糧仗。

translations.literal: Lun's chief administrator Wei Zhi, chief aide Jiang Lü, and others heard Lun still lived, raced to welcome him, and persuaded the refugee forts of seven palisades to supply grain and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's chief administrator Wei Zhi, chief aide Jiang Lü, and others heard he still lived, raced to welcome him, and persuaded the refugee forts of seven palisades to supply grain and arms.

sentences.zh: 綸出營巴水，流民八九千人附之，稍收散卒，屯於齊昌，遣使請降於齊，齊以綸為梁王。

translations.literal: Lun encamped on the Ba River; eight or nine thousand refugees attached to him; he gradually gathered scattered soldiers, encamped at Qichang, sent envoys to surrender to Qi, and Qi made Lun Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Lun encamped on the Ba River; eight or nine thousand refugees attached to him; he gradually gathered scattered soldiers, encamped at Qichang, sent envoys to surrender to Qi, and Qi made him Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹改封皇子大款為臨川王，大成為桂陽王，大封為汝南王。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Xiangdong changed enfeoffments, making imperial son Dakuan Prince of Linchuan, Dacheng Prince of Guiyang, and Dafeng Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong changed enfeoffments, making imperial son Dakuan Prince of Linchuan, Dacheng Prince of Guiyang, and Dafeng Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，魏軍至潼關。

translations.literal: On guihai, the Wei army reached Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the Wei army reached Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 庚午，齊主如晉陽，命太子殷居涼風堂監國。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Qi emperor went to Jinyang and ordered Crown Prince Yin to dwell in Liangfeng Hall and oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Qi emperor went to Jinyang and ordered Crown Prince Yin to dwell in Liangfeng Hall and oversee the state.

sentences.zh: 南郡王中兵參軍張彪等起兵於若邪山，攻破浙東諸縣，有眾數萬。

translations.literal: Central Army Adjutant Zhang Biao of the Prince of Nanjun and others raised troops on Mount Ruoye, stormed the eastern Zhe counties, and had a force of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Central army adjutant Zhang Biao of the Prince of Nanjun and others raised troops on Mount Ruoye, stormed the eastern Zhe counties, and mustered tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 吳郡人陸令公等說太守南海王大臨往依之。

translations.literal: Lu Linggong of Wu commandery and others urged Administrator Prince Dalin of Nanhai to go and rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Linggong of Wu commandery and others urged administrator Prince Dalin of Nanhai to join him.

sentences.zh: 大臨曰：「彪若成功，不資我力；

translations.literal: Dalin said, "If Biao succeeds, he will not need my strength.
translations.idiomatic: Dalin said, "If Biao succeeds, he will not need my strength.

sentences.zh: 如其橈敗，以我自解。

translations.literal: If he is broken and defeated, he will use me to excuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: If he is broken and defeated, he will use me to excuse himself.

sentences.zh: 不可往也。

translations.literal: I must not go.
translations.idiomatic: I must not go.

sentences.zh: 任約進寇西陽、武昌。

translations.literal: Ren Yue advanced to raid Xiyang and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue advanced to raid Xiyang and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 初，寧州刺史彭城徐文盛募兵數萬人討侯景，湘東王繹以為秦州刺史，使將兵東下，與約遇於武昌。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ningzhou Inspector Xu Wensheng of Pengcheng raised tens of thousands of men to attack Hou Jing; Prince Yi of Xiangdong made him Inspector of Qinzhou and had him lead troops east; he met Yue at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ningzhou inspector Xu Wensheng of Pengcheng raised tens of thousands to attack Hou Jing; Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong made him inspector of Qinzhou and had him lead troops east; he met Yue at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 繹以廬陵王應為江州刺史，以文盛為長史行府州事，督諸將拒之。

translations.literal: Yi made Prince Ying of Luling Inspector of Jiangzhou, made Wensheng Chief Administrator acting for headquarters and province, and had him supervise the generals in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Yi made Prince Ying of Luling inspector of Jiangzhou, made Wensheng chief administrator acting for headquarters and province, and had him supervise the generals in resistance.

sentences.zh: 應，續之子也。

translations.literal: Ying was Xu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was Xu's son.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸引齊兵未至，移營馬柵，距西陽八十里，任約聞之，遣儀同叱羅子通等將鐵騎二百襲之，綸不為備，策馬亡走。

translations.literal: Prince Lun of Shaoling had drawn Qi troops but they had not arrived; he moved camp to Mazha, eighty li from Xiyang; Ren Yue heard of it and sent Equal in Honor Chiluo Zitong and others with two hundred iron cavalry to surprise him; Lun made no preparations and fled on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Shaoling had drawn Qi troops but they had not arrived; he moved camp to Mazha, eighty li from Xiyang; Ren Yue heard and sent Chiluo Zitong, Equal in Honor, and others with two hundred iron cavalry to surprise him; Lun was caught unawares and fled on horseback.

sentences.zh: 時湘東王繹亦與齊連和，故齊人觀望，不助綸。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Yi of Xiangdong was also allied with Qi, so the Qi men watched and did not aid Lun.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong was also allied with Qi, so the Qi men held back and did not aid Lun.

sentences.zh: 定州刺史田祖龍迎綸，綸以祖龍為繹所厚，懼為所執，復歸齊昌。

translations.literal: Dingzhou Inspector Tian Zulong welcomed Lun; Lun, because Zulong was favored by Yi, feared he would be seized and returned to Qichang.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou inspector Tian Zulong welcomed Lun; Lun, because Zulong was favored by Yi, feared seizure and returned to Qichang.

sentences.zh: 行至汝南，魏所署汝南城主李素，綸之故吏也，開城納之，任約遂據西陽、武昌。

translations.literal: Reaching Runan, Li Su, city chief of Runan appointed by Wei and Lun's former clerk, opened the city and received him; Ren Yue then held Xiyang and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Runan, Li Su, city chief of Runan appointed by Wei and Lun's former clerk, opened the city and received him; Ren Yue then held Xiyang and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 裴之高帥子弟部曲千餘人至夏首，湘東王繹召之，以為新興、永守二郡太守。

translations.literal: Pei Zhigao led more than a thousand men of his clan retainers to Xiashou; Prince Yi of Xiangdong summoned him and made him Administrator of the two commanderies of Xinxing and Yongshou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhigao led more than a thousand clan retainers to Xiashou; Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong summoned him and made him administrator of Xinxing and Yongshou.

sentences.zh: 又以南平王恪為武州刺史，鎮武陵。

translations.literal: He also made Prince Ke of Nanping Inspector of Wuzhou and garrisoned Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Prince Ke of Nanping inspector of Wuzhou and garrisoned Wuling.

sentences.zh: 初，邵陵王綸以衡陽王獻為齊州刺史，鎮齊昌；

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince Lun of Shaoling had made Prince Xian of Hengyang Inspector of Qizhou and garrisoned Qichang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Lun of Shaoling had made Prince Xian of Hengyang inspector of Qizhou and garrisoned Qichang.

sentences.zh: 任約擊擒之，送建康，殺之。

translations.literal: Ren Yue struck, captured him, sent him to Jiankang, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue struck, captured him, sent him to Jiankang, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 獻，暢之孫也。

translations.literal: Xian was Chang's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was Chang's grandson.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，進侯景位相國，封二十郡，為漢王，加殊禮。

translations.literal: On yihai, Hou Jing was advanced to Chancellor of State, enfeoffed with twenty commanderies as Prince of Han, and granted extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Hou Jing was advanced to Chancellor of State, enfeoffed with twenty commanderies as Prince of Han, and granted extraordinary honors.

sentences.zh: 岳陽王察還襄陽。

translations.literal: Prince Cha of Yueyang returned to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cha of Yueyang returned to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 黎州民攻刺史張賁，賁棄城走。

translations.literal: The people of Lizhou attacked Inspector Zhang Ben; Ben abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Lizhou attacked inspector Zhang Ben; Ben abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 州民引氐酋北益州刺史楊法琛據黎州，命王、賈二姓詣武陵王紀請法琛為刺史。

translations.literal: The provincials brought in the Di chieftain Yang Fachen, Northern Yi Inspector, to hold Lizhou, and ordered the Wang and Jia clans to go to Prince Ji of Wuling and ask that Fachen be made inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The provincials brought in Di chieftain Yang Fachen, Northern Yi inspector, to hold Lizhou, and sent the Wang and Jia clans to Prince Ji of Wuling to ask that Fachen be made inspector.

sentences.zh: 紀深責之，囚法琛質子崇顒、崇虎。

translations.literal: Ji rebuked them severely and imprisoned Fachen's hostage sons Chongyan and Chonghu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji rebuked them severely and imprisoned Fachen's hostage sons Chongyan and Chonghu.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁丑朔，法琛遣使附魏。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day dingchou, Fachen sent envoys to submit to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day dingchou, Fachen sent envoys to submit to Wei.

sentences.zh: 己卯，齊主至晉陽宮。

translations.literal: On jimao, the Qi emperor reached Jinyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, the Qi emperor reached Jinyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 廣武王長弼與并州刺史段韶不協，齊主將如晉陽，長弼言於帝曰：「韶擁強兵在彼，恐不知人意，豈可徑往投之！

translations.literal: Prince Changbi of Guangwu was at odds with Bingzhou Inspector Duan Shao; as the Qi emperor was about to go to Jinyang, Changbi said to him, "Shao holds strong troops there and may not know men's hearts—how can you go straight and throw yourself upon him!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changbi of Guangwu was at odds with Bingzhou inspector Duan Shao; as the Qi emperor was about to go to Jinyang, Changbi said, "Shao holds strong troops there and may not read men's hearts—how can you go straight and throw yourself upon him!

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 既至，以長弼語告之，曰：「如君忠誠，人猶有讒，況其餘乎！

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he told Shao Changbi's words and said, "With loyalty like yours, men still slander you—how much more the rest!
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, he told Shao what Changbi had said: "With loyalty like yours, men still slander you—how much more the rest!

sentences.zh: 」長弼，永樂之弟也。

translations.literal: " Changbi was Yongle's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: " Changbi was Yongle's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以特進元韶為尚書左僕射，段韶為右僕射。

translations.literal: On yiyou, he made Special Advance Yuan Shao Left Vice Minister of Works and Duan Shao Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, he made Special Advance Yuan Shao Left Vice Minister of Works and Duan Shao Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 乙未，侯景自加宇宙大將軍、都督六合諸軍事，以詔文呈上。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Hou Jing on his own authority added Grand General of the Cosmos and Commander of All Military Affairs in the Six Directions, and presented the edict text to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Hou Jing on his own authority added Grand General of the Cosmos and Commander of All Military Affairs in the Six Directions, and presented the edict text to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上驚曰：「將軍乃有宇宙之號乎！

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and said, "General, you would even take a title of the cosmos!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled: "General, you would even take a title of the cosmos!

sentences.zh: 立皇子大鈞為西陽王，大威為武寧王，大球為建安王，大昕為義安王，大摯為綏建王，大圜為樂梁王。

translations.literal: He made imperial sons Dajun Prince of Xiyang, Dawei Prince of Wuning, Daqiu Prince of Jian'an, Daxin Prince of Yi'an, Dazhi Prince of Suijian, and Dayuan Prince of Leliang.
translations.idiomatic: He made imperial sons Dajun Prince of Xiyang, Dawei Prince of Wuning, Daqiu Prince of Jian'an, Daxin Prince of Yi'an, Dazhi Prince of Suijian, and Dayuan Prince of Leliang.

sentences.zh: 齊東徐州刺史行台辛術鎮下邳。

translations.literal: Eastern Xuzhou Inspector and Mobile Headquarters Xin Shu of Qi garrisoned Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Xuzhou inspector and mobile headquarters Xin Shu of Qi garrisoned Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，侯景征租入建康，術帥眾度淮斷之，燒其谷百萬石，遂圍陽平，景行台郭元建引兵救之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Hou Jing levied grain rents into Jiankang; Shu led his force across the Huai to cut them off, burned a million shi of grain, then besieged Yangping; Jing's mobile headquarters Guo Yuanjian led troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Hou Jing levied grain rents into Jiankang; Shu led his force across the Huai to cut them off, burned a million shi of grain, then besieged Yangping; Hou Jing's mobile headquarters Guo Yuanjian led troops to rescue it.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，術略三千餘家，還下邳。

translations.literal: On renxu, Shu raided more than three thousand households and returned to Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Shu raided more than three thousand households and returned to Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 武陵王紀帥諸軍發成都，湘東王繹遣使以書止之曰：「蜀人勇悍，易動難安，弟可鎮之，吾自當滅賊。

translations.literal: Prince Ji of Wuling led the armies out from Chengdu; Prince Yi of Xiangdong sent envoys with a letter stopping him, saying, "The men of Shu are fierce and hard to settle once stirred; younger brother, you can hold them—I myself will destroy the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Wuling led the armies out from Chengdu; Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong sent envoys with a letter stopping him: "The men of Shu are fierce and hard to settle once stirred; younger brother, hold them—I myself will destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 」又別紙云：「地擬孫、劉，各安境界；

translations.literal: " On a separate sheet he wrote, "Our lands may be compared to Sun and Liu—each keeps his border.
translations.idiomatic: " On a separate sheet he wrote, "Our lands may be compared to Sun and Liu—each keeps his border.

sentences.zh: 情深魯、衛，書信恆通。

translations.literal: Our bond is deep as Lu and Wei—letters should always pass.
translations.idiomatic: Our bond is deep as Lu and Wei—letters should always pass.

sentences.zh: 甲子，南平王恪帥文武拜箋推湘東王繹為相國，總百揆；

translations.literal: On jiazi, Prince Ke of Nanping led civil and military officials in a memorial urging Prince Yi of Xiangdong as Chancellor of State to oversee the hundred duties.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Prince Ke of Nanping led civil and military officials in a memorial urging Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong as Chancellor of State to oversee the hundred duties.

sentences.zh: 繹不許。

translations.literal: Yi refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yi refused.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相泰自弘農為橋，濟河，至建州。

translations.literal: Wei Chancellor Tai built a bridge from Hongnong, crossed the river, and reached Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yuwen Tai built a bridge from Hongnong, crossed the river, and reached Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，齊主自將出頓東城。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Qi emperor personally led the army out and encamped at East City.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the Qi emperor personally led the army out and encamped at East City.

sentences.zh: 泰聞其軍容嚴盛，歎曰：「高歡不死矣！

translations.literal: Tai heard his army's bearing was stern and grand and sighed, "Gao Huan is not dead after all!
translations.idiomatic: Tai heard his army's bearing was stern and grand and sighed, "Gao Huan is not dead after all!

sentences.zh: 」會久雨，自秋及冬，魏軍畜產多死，乃自蒲阪還。

translations.literal: " It happened that long rains lasted from autumn into winter; many of the Wei army's livestock died, and they returned from Puban.
translations.idiomatic: " Long rains lasted from autumn into winter; much of the Wei army's livestock died, and they returned from Puban.

sentences.zh: 於是河南自洛陽，河北自平陽已東，皆入於齊。

translations.literal: Thereupon south of the river from Luoyang and north of the river from east of Pingyang all entered Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon south of the river from Luoyang and north of the river from east of Pingyang all fell to Qi.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，徐文盛軍貝磯，任約帥水軍逆戰，文盛大破之，斬叱羅子通、趙威方，仍進軍大舉口。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Xu Wensheng's army was at Beiji; Ren Yue led the water force to meet in battle; Wensheng routed him, beheaded Chiluo Zitong and Zhao Weifang, and advanced to Dajukou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Xu Wensheng's army was at Beiji; Ren Yue led the water force to meet him; Wensheng routed him, beheaded Chiluo Zitong and Zhao Weifang, and advanced to Dajukou.

sentences.zh: 侯景遣宋子仙等將兵二萬助約，以約守西陽，久不能進，自出屯晉熙。

translations.literal: Hou Jing sent Song Zixian and others with twenty thousand troops to aid Yue, had Yue hold Xiyang, and when he could not advance for long, went out himself to encamp at Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sent Song Zixian and others with twenty thousand troops to aid Yue, had Yue hold Xiyang, and when progress stalled, went out himself to encamp at Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 南康王會理以建康空虛，與太子左衛將軍柳敬禮、西鄉侯勸、東鄉侯勉謀起兵誅王偉。

translations.literal: Prince Huili of Nankang, because Jiankang was empty, with Crown Prince Left Guard General Liu Jingli, Marquis Quan of Xixiang, and Marquis Mian of Dongxiang plotted to raise troops and kill Wang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huili of Nankang, because Jiankang was empty, with crown prince left guard general Liu Jingli, Marquis Quan of Xixiang, and Marquis Mian of Dongxiang plotted to raise troops and kill Wang Wei.

sentences.zh: 安樂侯乂理出奔長蘆，集眾得千餘人。

translations.literal: Marquis Yili of Anle fled to Changlu, gathered followers, and had more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Yili of Anle fled to Changlu, gathered followers, and mustered more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 建安侯賁、中宿世子子邕知其謀，以告偉。

translations.literal: Marquis Ben of Jian'an and Heir Ziyong of Zhongsu learned of the plot and reported it to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Ben of Jian'an and heir Ziyong of Zhongsu learned of the plot and reported it to Wei.

sentences.zh: 偉收會理、敬禮、勸、勉及會理弟祁陽侯通理，俱殺之。

translations.literal: Wei seized Huili, Jingli, Quan, Mian, and Huili's younger brother Marquis Tongli of Qiyang, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wei seized Huili, Jingli, Quan, Mian, and Huili's younger brother Marquis Tongli of Qiyang, and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 乂理為左右所殺。

translations.literal: Yili was killed by his own followers.
translations.idiomatic: Yili was killed by his own followers.

sentences.zh: 錢塘褚冕，以會理故舊，捶掠千計，終無異言。

translations.literal: Chu Mian of Qiantang, because of old ties with Huili, was beaten more than a thousand strokes yet to the end spoke no different word.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Mian of Qiantang, because of old ties with Huili, was beaten more than a thousand strokes yet never spoke a different word.

sentences.zh: 會理隔壁謂之曰：「褚郎，卿豈不為我致此？

translations.literal: Huili in the next cell said to him, "Master Chu, did you not bring this upon me?
translations.idiomatic: Huili in the next cell said to him, "Master Chu, did you not bring this upon me?

sentences.zh: 卿雖忍死明我，我心實欲殺賊！

translations.literal: Though you endure death to clear me, in my heart I truly wished to kill the rebels!
translations.idiomatic: Though you endure death to clear me, in my heart I truly wished to kill the rebels!

sentences.zh: 」冕竟不服，景乃宥之。

translations.literal: " Mian to the end would not submit; Jing then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " Mian to the end would not submit; Hou Jing then pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 勸，昺之子；

translations.literal: Quan was Bing's son.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was Bing's son.

sentences.zh: 賁，正德之弟子；

translations.literal: Ben was Zhengde's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Ben was Zhengde's nephew.

sentences.zh: 子邕，憺之孫也。

translations.literal: Ziyong was Dan's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong was Dan's grandson.

sentences.zh: 帝自即位以來，景防衛甚嚴，外人莫得進見，唯武林侯諮及僕射王克、舍人殷不害，並以文弱得出入臥內，帝與之講論而已。

translations.literal: Since the emperor took the throne, Jing's guard had been very strict and outsiders could not gain audience; only Marquis Zi of Wulin and Vice Minister Wang Ke and Attendant Yin Buhai, all frail in manner, could enter the sleeping quarters, and the emperor discussed texts with them—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor took the throne, Hou Jing's guard had been very strict and outsiders could not gain audience; only Marquis Zi of Wulin, vice minister Wang Ke, and attendant Yin Buhai, all frail in manner, could enter the sleeping quarters, and the emperor discussed texts with them—that was all.

sentences.zh: 及會理死，克、不害懼禍，稍自疏。

translations.literal: When Huili died, Ke and Buhai feared disaster and gradually kept their distance.
translations.idiomatic: When Huili died, Ke and Buhai feared disaster and gradually kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 咨獨不離帝，朝請無絕；

translations.literal: Zi alone did not leave the emperor; morning audiences never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Zi alone did not leave the emperor; morning audiences never ceased.

sentences.zh: 景惡之，使其仇人刁戍刺殺咨於廣莫門外。

translations.literal: Jing hated this and had his enemy Diao Shu assassinate Zi outside the Guangmo Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing hated this and had his enemy Diao Shu assassinate Zi outside the Guangmo Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝之即位也，景與帝登重雲殿，禮佛為誓云：「自今君臣兩無猜貳，臣固不負陛下，陛下亦不得負臣！

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Jing and the emperor ascended Chongyun Hall, worshipped the Buddha, and swore, saying, "From now on lord and minister shall harbor no mutual suspicion; your servant surely will not fail Your Majesty, and Your Majesty must not fail your servant!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Hou Jing and the emperor ascended Chongyun Hall, worshipped the Buddha, and swore: "From now on lord and minister shall harbor no mutual suspicion; your servant will not fail Your Majesty, and Your Majesty must not fail your servant!

sentences.zh: 」及會理謀洩，景疑帝知之，故殺咨。

translations.literal: " When Huili's plot leaked, Jing suspected the emperor knew and therefore killed Zi.
translations.idiomatic: " When Huili's plot leaked, Hou Jing suspected the emperor knew and therefore killed Zi.

sentences.zh: 帝自知不久，指所居殿謂殷不害曰：「龐涓當死此下。

translations.literal: The emperor knew he would not last long, pointed at the hall where he dwelt, and told Yin Buhai, "Pang Juan ought to die beneath this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew he would not last long, pointed at the hall where he dwelt, and told Yin Buhai, "Pang Juan ought to die beneath this.

sentences.zh: 景自帥眾討楊白華於宣城，白華力屈而降，景以其北人，全之，以為左民尚書，誅其兄子彬以報來亮之怨。

translations.literal: Jing himself led the host to attack Yang Baihua at Xuancheng; Baihua, strength exhausted, surrendered; Jing, because he was a northerner, spared him and made him Minister of the Left People, but executed his elder brother's son Bin to repay Lai Liang's grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing himself led the host to attack Yang Baihua at Xuancheng; Baihua, strength exhausted, surrendered; Hou Jing, because he was a northerner, spared him and made him Minister of the Left People, but executed his elder brother's son Bin to repay Lai Liang's grudge.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙子朔，景封建安侯賁為竟陵王，中宿世子子邕為隨王，仍賜姓侯氏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day bingzi, Jing enfeoffed Marquis Ben of Jian'an as Prince of Jingling and Heir Ziyong of Zhongsu as Prince of Sui, and further granted the surname Hou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day bingzi, Hou Jing enfeoffed Marquis Ben of Jian'an as Prince of Jingling and heir Ziyong of Zhongsu as Prince of Sui, and further granted the surname Hou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，齊主還鄴。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Qi emperor returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the Qi emperor returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸在汝南，修城池，集士卒，將圖安陸。

translations.literal: Prince Lun of Shaoling was at Runan, repaired walls and moats, gathered soldiers, and intended to take Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Shaoling was at Runan, repaired walls and moats, gathered soldiers, and intended to take Anlu.

sentences.zh: 魏安州刺史馬祐以告丞相泰，泰遣楊忠將萬人救安陸。

translations.literal: Wei Anzhou Inspector Ma You reported to Chancellor Tai; Tai sent Yang Zhong with ten thousand men to rescue Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Anzhou inspector Ma You reported to Chancellor Tai; Tai sent Yang Zhong with ten thousand men to rescue Anlu.

sentences.zh: 武陵王紀遣潼州刺史楊乾運、南梁州刺史譙淹合兵二萬討楊法琛，法琛發兵據劍閣以拒之。

translations.literal: Prince Ji of Wuling sent Tongzhou Inspector Yang Qianyun and Nanliangzhou Inspector Qiao Yan with a combined force of twenty thousand to attack Yang Fachen; Fachen raised troops and held Jiange Pass to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Wuling sent Tongzhou inspector Yang Qianyun and Nanliangzhou inspector Qiao Yan with twenty thousand men to attack Yang Fachen; Fachen raised troops and held Jiange Pass to resist.

sentences.zh: 侯景還建康。

translations.literal: Hou Jing returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 初，魏敬宗以爾朱榮為柱國大將軍，位在丞相上；

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Jingzong of Wei had made Erzhu Rong Grand General of the Pillars, rank above the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Jingzong of Wei had made Erzhu Rong Grand General of the Pillars, rank above the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 榮敗，此官遂廢。

translations.literal: When Rong was defeated, the office was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was defeated, the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，文帝復以丞相泰為之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Emperor Wen again made Chancellor Tai holder of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, Emperor Wen again made Chancellor Tai holder of it.

sentences.zh: 其後功參佐命，望實俱重者，亦居此官，凡八人，曰安定公宇文泰，廣陵王欣，趙郡公李弼，隴西公李虎，河內公獨孤信，南陽公趙貴，常山公於謹，彭城公侯莫陳崇，謂之八柱國。

translations.literal: Thereafter those whose merit shared in founding the mandate and whose repute and substance were both weighty also held this office—eight in all: Duke of Anding Yuwen Tai, Prince Xin of Guangling, Duke of Zhaojun Li Bi, Duke of Longxi Li Hu, Duke of Henei Dugu Xin, Duke of Nanyang Zhao Gui, Duke of Changshan Yu Jin, and Duke of Pengcheng Hou Mo Chen Chong—called the Eight Pillars.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter those whose merit shared in founding the mandate and whose repute and substance were both weighty also held this office—eight in all: Duke of Anding Yuwen Tai, Prince Xin of Guangling, Duke of Zhaojun Li Bi, Duke of Longxi Li Hu, Duke of Henei Dugu Xin, Duke of Nanyang Zhao Gui, Duke of Changshan Yu Jin, and Duke of Pengcheng Hou Mo Chen Chong—the Eight Pillars.

sentences.zh: 泰始籍民之才力者為府兵，身租庸調，一切蠲之，以農隙講閱戰陳，馬畜糧備，六家供之；

translations.literal: Tai first registered men of talent and strength among the people as garrison soldiers, exempting them entirely from body-tax, corvée, and cloth levies; in the gaps of farming they drilled battle formations; horses, livestock, grain, and stores were supplied by six households.
translations.idiomatic: Tai first registered men of talent and strength as garrison soldiers, exempting them entirely from body-tax, corvée, and cloth levies; in the gaps of farming they drilled battle formations; horses, livestock, grain, and stores were supplied by six households.

sentences.zh: 合為百府，每府一郎將主之，分屬二十四軍。

translations.literal: They were combined into a hundred garrisons, each garrison with one commandant in charge, divided among twenty-four armies.
translations.idiomatic: They were combined into a hundred garrisons, each with one commandant in charge, divided among twenty-four armies.

sentences.zh: 泰任總百揆，督中外諸軍；

translations.literal: Tai held overall charge of the hundred duties and supervised all forces inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Tai held overall charge of the hundred duties and supervised all forces inside and outside.

sentences.zh: 欣以宗室宿望，從容禁闥而已。

translations.literal: Xin, by imperial clan and long-standing repute, merely moved at ease within the inner gates.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, by imperial clan and long-standing repute, merely moved at ease within the inner gates.

sentences.zh: 餘六人各督二大將軍，凡十二大將軍，每大將軍各統開府二人，開府各領一軍。

translations.literal: The remaining six each supervised two grand generals—twelve grand generals in all; each grand general in turn commanded two opening offices, and each opening office led one army.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining six each supervised two grand generals—twelve in all; each grand general commanded two opening offices, and each opening office led one army.

sentences.zh: 是後功臣位至柱國大將軍、開府儀同三司、儀同三司者甚眾，率為散官，無所統御，雖有繼掌其事者，聞望皆出諸公之下雲。

translations.literal: After this, meritorious men reaching Grand General of the Pillars, Opening Office Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, or Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes were very many; mostly they were nominal offices with nothing to command; even when successors held the posts, their fame and standing all fell below these lords.
translations.idiomatic: After this, meritorious men reaching Grand General of the Pillars, Opening Office Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, or Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes were very many; mostly they were nominal offices with nothing to command; even when successors held the posts, their fame and standing all fell below these lords.

sentences.zh: 齊主命散騎侍郎宋景業造《天保歷》，行之。

translations.literal: The Qi emperor ordered Direct Attendant Song Jingye to compose the Tianbao Calendar, and it was put in use.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor ordered direct attendant Song Jingye to compose the Tianbao Calendar, and it was put in use.
